## 0.404.0

### Minor Changes

- 7123167: New job trigger `{ maintenance: true }`: one daily run in the app's maintenance window (`KUMIKO_MAINTENANCE_WINDOW`, `HH:MM` UTC, default 03:00), so a sleeping app wakes once a day for all its cleanup jobs. The cleanup jobs of the framework and the bundled features use it.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: types
  type: improvement
  title: JobTrigger gains { maintenance: true }
  detail: A job with trigger { maintenance: true } runs once a day at the maintenance window of the app. Prefer it over a fixed cron for housekeeping; the window can be set per app.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Maintenance trigger and KUMIKO_MAINTENANCE_WINDOW
  detail: The job runner registers maintenance jobs as a daily UTC scheduler at JobRunnerOptions.maintenanceWindow (default 03:00), set from KUMIKO_MAINTENANCE_WINDOW by runProdApp and runWorkerApp; an invalid value aborts the boot. maintenanceWindowFromEnv is exported from the jobs barrel. files sweep-orphaned-uploads (hourly before) and the soft-delete cleanup jobs (03:00 and 03:15 before) now run in the window. A schedule stored with the old time is replaced on the next start.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: jobs
  type: improvement
  title: Cleanup jobs run once a day in the maintenance window
  detail: jobs (stale-run-sweep, hourly before, and retention-cleanup), user-data-rights (export and forget), data-retention, audit escape-hatch-retention, inbound-mail retention, delivery attempt-log-retention and form-draft cleanup use trigger { maintenance: true } instead of 03:00 to 03:30 and hourly crons. Without KUMIKO_MAINTENANCE_WINDOW they all run at 03:00 UTC. A stuck job run is now marked failed at most a day after it crosses the stale timeout.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: feature-ast
  type: improvement
  title: Pattern library documents the maintenance trigger
  detail: The job pattern's comment and summary name { maintenance: true }; the parser already reads it as a literal option.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 7123167: Apps sharing one Redis can be confined to a per-app ACL user: `KUMIKO_REDIS_PREFIX` puts every key, the BullMQ queues and every Pub/Sub channel under `<prefix>:`, and `KUMIKO_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` lets a SIGTERM wait for running jobs.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: KUMIKO_REDIS_PREFIX namespaces all Redis keys and channels
  detail: redisNamespaceFromEnv resolves keyPrefix, bullmqPrefix, channelPrefix and the subscribe pattern. Unset keeps today's layout (bull:*, unprefixed locks, rate limit, idempotency and cache keys). Set, the main ioredis client gets keyPrefix <P>:, the job runner passes prefix <P>:bull to every Queue and Worker (new JobRunnerOptions.redisNamespace, also on the entrypoint jobs block) and gives its lock client the keyPrefix, and the SSE broker, cache-sync bus and toggle signal use <P>: channels. Redis matches PSUBSCRIBE patterns literally against ACL channel rules, so with a prefix they subscribe to <P>:* and filter by channel. A value with ":" or glob characters, or a KUMIKO_REDIS_CHANNEL_PREFIX that differs from it, aborts the boot. The cache-sync bus of runProdApp, runWorkerApp and createDefaultCacheSyncBus now also honours KUMIKO_REDIS_CHANNEL_PREFIX alone (before, only SSE and toggle channels did). JobRunner gains an optional stopConsuming(), which createJobRunner implements. The ACL rule set and the key layout for a wake-up service are in docs/reference/infra-requirements.md.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: runProdApp and runWorkerApp use the Redis prefix and drain running jobs on SIGTERM
  detail: Both boots pass the namespace to the Redis client, the cache-sync bus and the job runner, so enqueuer and consumer share one key space. KUMIKO_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS (positive integer, invalid aborts the boot) sets the drain budget; signals.drainTimeoutMs wins, the default stays 25 s. Entrypoint stop() now stops every job lane fetching first, then waits for active jobs up to that budget before the database and Redis close; before, the lifecycle's fixed 40 s cut the wait short.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: feature-toggles
  type: improvement
  title: Feature-toggle Redis signal follows KUMIKO_REDIS_PREFIX
  detail: createRedisToggleSyncSignal takes an optional channelSubscribePattern (default from KUMIKO_REDIS_PREFIX) and ignores messages from other channels, which a prefix-wide subscription delivers.
  -->

  type: breaking
  title: Agent manifest labels are one string in the requested locale
  detail: `buildAgentManifest` used to emit every label in every locale (`labels: { de, en, es }`, often `{}`), although the caller names one `locale`. Entities, fields, navs and workspaces now carry `label?: string`, screens `title?: string`, picked in the requested locale, then English, then the first other locale, and left out when untranslated.   migration: Read `entity.label`, `field.label`, `nav.label`, `workspace.label` and `screen.title` instead of the `labels`/`titles` maps. Code that only passes the manifest to `buildToolCatalog` or serialises it needs no change.

### Patch Changes

- 6fd7cbc: Boot rules get stable ids. The measured hot spots (PII and retention, entityList, i18n, card meta columns, action icons, API and extension wiring, feature bootChecks, user-data-rights hooks) throw typed rule errors and report every violation of a run instead of the first. `agents/boot-rules.md` lists every rule with summary and fix, and the new `boot-raw-throws` guard keeps raw throws in boot validation from growing.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Boot violations carry rule ids with a fix and a doc link
  detail: 43 boot rules have an id such as `pii/subject-key-sortable` or `entity-list/default-sort-required`. A violation in `BootValidationError.violations` and in `kumiko-schema validate` (text and `--json`) carries that id instead of `unclassified/<check>`, plus a `Fix:` line and `Rule: agents/boot-rules.md#<id>`. PII field rules, entityList screen rules, missing i18n keys, API and extension usages and user-data-rights hooks now report all violations in one run. Message texts are unchanged. `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine` exports `bootRuleError`, `BootRuleViolation`, `BootValidationError`, `collectBootRuleViolations` and the types `BootRule`, `BootRuleTable`, `BootViolation`, so a feature's `r.bootCheck` can throw a classified rule.

- dd2b30f: The system-check history lists the newest run first even when two runs start in the same second.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: readiness
  type: fix
  title: System-check history keeps runs of the same second in order
  detail: `probe-run:list` returned `requestedAt` as `Instant.toString()`, which drops trailing zeros in the fraction, and `pageRows` sorts that field as a string. Two runs in the same second could then come out reversed (`…:20Z` sorted after `…:20.001Z`), so the history showed the older run on top and a click opened it. `requestedAt` now always carries six fractional digits, so string order matches time order.
  -->

## 0.401.0

### Minor Changes

- a11ae25: files: `rebindFileRef` moves a bound file onto another record's file field. readGate: `allLinks` needs every link readable; documents opts in with `linkReadMode`. The documents tab points at `filed-document`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: rebindFileRef, readGate allLinks with documents linkReadMode, documents tab entity fix
  detail: `rebindFileRef(ctx, { fileRefId, from, to })` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/files` moves a file that is already bound (for example to an upload record or an inbound mail) onto another record's file field, for server code where a record takes over that file; pending uploads keep using `bindPendingFileRef`. It finds only files of the caller's tenant ("not-found" otherwise), answers "moved" when the file no longer sits at `from`, "rebound" when it was moved or already sits at `to`, and "version-conflict" when a parallel bind committed first, because the update is checked against the stream version. The target must be a registered file field whose accept and maxSize the file fits. A caller other than the framework system user must be able to read the file and must be able to write both the source record and field (not locked; an entity without update handler leaves the move to the system user) and the target record and field; the source row stays locked until the transaction commits, so a lock set in between is either seen or waits; a system job (`{ db, registry, user: ctx.systemUser }`) skips these checks, but the target record must exist. Rebind first, then save the id into the target field; clearing or deleting the source record afterwards leaves the file alone. An entity `readGate` takes `allLinks` as an alternative to `anyLink`: a row with links is visible only when the viewer can read every live link, and the boot validator rejects a gate that declares both. `createDocumentsFeature({ linkReadMode: "allLinks" })` switches the documents gate to it; the default stays `anyLink`, and the file-owner part is unchanged. `documentsTab()` now references `documents:filed-document`; before, a projection screen using it failed boot after the entity rename. Linking a document to a target entity without an update handler is now allowed for the roles in that entity's `access.write` (plus its row-level write rule); a target with neither stays unlinkable. `documents:write:link` and `documents:write:unlink` have title and field-label translations (de, en), and the documents write handlers carry an explicit `agent.risk` (link, unlink, create, update "mid"; import "high"). `createDocumentsFeature({ categoryLabels })` takes a de/en label per category (an unlabelled one shows its raw value); a key that is not in `categories` throws.
  -->
- 2ee38e5: framework: `createReferenceField`, boot checks for user references and file `accept`, opt-in `requireFieldValueTranslations`, typed phase slots on entity handlers.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Boot rejects a user reference with personal: false and file accept entries that never match
  detail: `createReferenceField({ entity, personal?, reason?, required? })` builds a foreign key; a target ending in `:user` defaults to `personal: "ref"` and throws on `personal: false`. The boot validator now rejects a reference field to the user entity that carries `personal: false`, and a file, files, image or images field (also inside embedded schemas) whose `accept` has an entry that is not a bare lower-case extension, because the upload check compares the file's extension only. The new boot option `requireFieldValueTranslations: true` (also readable from the schema CLI input) lists every missing translation of select/multiSelect options and embedded cell labels shown by entityList/entityEdit screens in one error. `defineEntityWriteHandler` and the create/update/delete/restore wrappers return a type whose `reserveBeforeTransaction`, `beforeTransaction` and `beforeTransactionWhenNested` are `undefined`, so a handler spread into `defineWriteHandler` can add its own. user-data-rights has the export-job status option labels (de, en, es, fr, it); managed-pages branding accepts `png, jpg, jpeg, webp` instead of MIME types.
  migration: Replace `personal: false` on a reference to the user entity with `createReferenceField({ entity: "user:user" })` or `personal: "ref"`. Write `accept` entries as bare extensions (`"pdf"`, not `".pdf"` or `"application/pdf"`).
  -->

## 0.400.0

### Minor Changes

- fa62e07: Derived fields can be computed in SQL and sorted, relatedList tabs follow query access and can count from their own query.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: SQL derived fields, query-gated relatedList tabs, count badge
  detail: A derived field with `sql` (coalesce over fields, or a related-table count, countDistinct or first with optional label and conditions incl. activeOn/today/now) is computed inside the list SELECT and may set `sortable: true`, also as entityList defaultSort; JS `derive` fields stay display-only and read the SQL values. Related rows and measured fields respect the viewer's read access, a gated value is NULL. GET /api/schema removes relatedList sections (tabs, entityEdit sections, expandableRow) whose query the caller's roles cannot run, and metrics linking to a removed tab lose their navigate. `count: true` on a relatedList tab shows the tab badge from the section's own query total. A metric only becomes clickable when its entityId target resolves, and groupBy labels now also resolve for entities with a backingTable. `valueType: "money"` is allowed for a SQL derived `related` + `first` on a money field: amount and currency are read together and the row carries the stored money shape (no key when unset), sorting is by minor units. Ownership where-rules of a label target or related table are qualified with the subquery's own alias (a label of a row the viewer cannot read no longer leaks when the target is the outer entity), the related entity and label target must also be readable through a query handler of the viewer's roles, backingTable entities are read from their real table (also for reference labels, reference search and label sort, which returned a 500 before), an entity may derive from itself, and a sortable related derived field needs an index on the join column.
  -->
- d8c43e7: New `documents` bundled feature and an entity `readGate` so a record can be visible only through links to other records and the owner of its file.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Entity readGate and the documents feature
  detail: `createEntity({ readGate: { anyLink, fileOwner, linkExemptRoles } })` hides a row unless the viewer can read at least one linked host (join rows with a parentRef) and the owner of the referenced file; it is applied in list, detail, eager-load and relation reads, fail-closed without the registry, and the framework system user passes. Hand-written list/detail handlers for a gated entity are rejected at boot, live signals for gated entities stay anonymous. `ParentVisibilityOption` gains `canReadEntity` and `resolveTable`. The new `documents` feature (`createDocumentsFeature({ categories, linkTargets, capture?, retention? })`) files documents with category, issue and expiry date, links them to records (link, unlink, for-record and per-type queries, expiry overview), lists them on the `documents:screen:list` projection list through `documents:query:overview` (an `expiry` state per row and an "expiring" filter that returns expired and soon-expiring documents), captures files saved into configured entity fields via a postSave hook, and offers an idempotent SYSTEM-only import for jobs. Updating or deleting a document needs write access to one of its linked hosts (admin roles and the system user are exempt). Reference search and sort on a readGate target now apply the gate, and `parentVisibilityFor` decides `canReadEntity` by the entity's own detail query, the same rule the file route uses, so a `liveEntities` query no longer widens what a file owner shows. A document cannot claim another user's unbound upload. A document never defaults its title to the file name.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Hooks run for handlers that return response data; readOnly related lists
  detail: A write handler wrapped by `withResponseData` (for example `tenant:write:remove-member`) lost its lifecycle result, so postSave/postDelete hooks and projections were skipped. `WriteResult` now carries an optional `lifecycle` that the dispatcher and batch flush use and that is stripped from client responses. `EditRelatedListSection` gains `readOnly: true` for plain tables without an entity; the boot validator rejects it together with rowClick/rowActions and guard R2 skips it. The bin test helpers and `envWithoutGitOverrides` now also strip GIT_COMMON_DIR and the other git location variables.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: An untouched money field is no longer submitted as 0
  detail: Forms seed a money field with its currency only and drop that currency-only value on submit, so a handler can tell a deliberately typed 0 from an untouched field. A currency-only value counts as missing for required checks, and the input shows empty instead of 0.00; config forms keep their plain-number contract.
  migration: A form that left a required money field untouched used to submit 0 and now fails validation; type the amount (also in e2e and DOM tests) or give the field a value through `load` or the record. Handlers that read an absent optional money field as 0 must default it themselves.
  -->
- 10ee71d: documents: the entities are named `filed-document` and `filed-document-link`, the import refuses a foreign id, and access splits into read, write and delete.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: documents entities are filed-document and filed-document-link; safe import; split access
  detail: The documents feature registers its entities as `filed-document` (table `read_filed_documents`) and `filed-document-link` (table `read_filed_document_links`), so an app that has its own `document` entity keeps its events and tables; handler and query names follow (`documents:write:filed-document:create`, `documents:query:filed-document:list`, `documents:query:filed-document-link:list`), and so do the field label keys `documents:entity:filed-document:field:*`. `documents:write:import` now fails with a conflict (`documents.errors.import-id-taken`) and links nothing when the id is already used by a stream that is not a document; a repeat import of the same document, deleted or not, still changes nothing; the check reads the stream, so a row-level `readAccess` cannot turn a retry into a refusal. With `readAccess` set, the system user keeps reading every document, so capture and import still find the ones the rule hides. An imported document's createdAt is the time of the import, because the event store does not backdate events; issuedAt carries the business date. `createDocumentsFeature({ access })` takes either one rule for everything, as before, or `{ read, write, delete }` (type `DocumentsAccess`): read covers the lists, detail, for-record, the overviews and the list screen, write covers create, update, link and unlink; a missing read or write keeps the TenantAdmin and TenantMember default and a missing delete follows write. The readGate on the document is unchanged.
  -->
- e742383: Embedded lists work as phone inspection checklists: photos per row, limit checks, conditional fields and touch-friendly cards.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Embedded list as inspection checklist
  detail: Every entity field and every embedded sub-field takes `visibleWhen` and `requiredWhen` (FieldCondition). The executor enforces `requiredWhen` on create and update; it returns `validation_error` with paths like `checkpoints.0.finding`, and on update it only checks fields whose value or condition field changed. A field is required only while it is visible, and hidden values are kept. Embedded sub-fields can be `images` (with `capture`) or `files` (`maxSize`, `accept`, `maxCount`). Uploads send `subField` next to `fieldName`, and `file_refs.fieldName` stays the embedded field, so binding, tenant check, disposal, read access, GDPR forget and retention work as for top-level file fields. The new derived op `inRange` (`from: [value, min, max]`, `inside`, `outside`) writes into a select sub-field. Any derived cell can carry a row-level `when`, and server and client compute through the same `withDerivedCells`. Select sub-fields take `optionTones`; segments show the tone of the selected option, and narrow screens render cards with 44px controls and the read-only label as the card title. Boot validates the condition fields and rejects `required: true` combined with `visibleWhen`/`requiredWhen`. Saving now enforces `access.write` on embedded sub-fields per row (`ownership_denied`, path `field.subField`); before, only the read side honored sub-field access. Saving also checks each newly placed file id against the `accept`/`maxSize` of the sub-field it lands in (`file_violates_bind_target`). Boot also rejects a numeric derived op whose target is not numeric, which can break an app that derived into a text or select cell. Recipe: `samples/recipes/inspection-checklist`.
  -->

  BillingFoundationOptions.authorizeOneOffCheckout runs before every one-off (mode payment) checkout, after the oneOffPriceIds gate and before any provider call. A rejection becomes an UnprocessableError with the hook's reason as code. Without the hook the behavior is unchanged.

  create-checkout-session with mode payment and no providerCustomerId now passes the customer id of the tenant's own subscription at the same provider, so Stripe also receives the customer on one-off checkouts. The foreign-customer guard still applies.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes

  type: improvement
  title: One-off checkouts reuse the tenant's provider customer
  -->

  PaymentEvent.quantity (absent means 1) reaches the stored payment-received event payload, which stays readable for events stored before. Apps that grant credits per pack have to multiply by it. No read-model column.

  feature: files
  type: improvement

A handler that lists or links files no longer needs its own copy of the rule.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: beforeTransactionWhenNested skip lets a handler with a beforeTransaction phase run nested
  detail: `beforeTransactionWhenNested: "skip"` on a write handler lets a nested ctx.dispatch.write run it without the phase. `event.prepared` is then `undefined` (typed `TPrepared | undefined`) and the handler does that work inside its own transaction. Top-level commands still run the phase. Without the option a nested call stays rejected. Boot rejects the option without beforeTransaction and together with reserveBeforeTransaction; transaction "perCommand" is already rejected next to beforeTransaction.

  detail: A catch-up job consumer now filters on the trigger's event types before the stored event is upcast, so a foreign event with a failing upcaster no longer stalls the job cursor. Boot rejects `trigger.catchUp` together with `maxPerTenant` onLimit "skip" (including the number shorthand): a replay must not discard history. Use onLimit "defer".

The registry gets getReadModelEntity and getReadModelEntityOwner; two projections declaring an entity for the same source fail the boot. POST /files still accepts only r.entity targets, so a client can never attach to a read model. deleteFileRefsBoundToRecord soft-deletes the fileRefs of one record for owners that remove it without an r.entity delete.

- 9c4e277: Imported mails keep their full text, the original and their attachments. A mail the provider cannot parse no longer blocks a mailbox, a mailbox that stops syncing says so, a disconnected mailbox can come back without duplicates, and a new or reactivated mailbox syncs right away.

  title: A hanging mailbox no longer blocks the others
  detail: The supervisor syncs up to 4 accounts at the same time (pollConcurrency), skips an account whose previous sync is still running, and abandons a sync after 10 minutes (accountPollDeadlineMs) as one failed poll; plugin.fetch and plugin.fetchContent receive an AbortSignal, and an abandoned sync stores nothing and moves no cursor. The IMAP client sets connection (20 s) and greeting (16 s) timeouts explicitly.
  -->

  feature: jobs
  type: improvement
  title: r.job event triggers can catch up on stored events
  detail: trigger { on, catchUp: true } gives the job its own event consumer job:<jobQn> that starts at the beginning of the event store, so events from before the job existed run it too, once per event (job id derived from job QN and event id). Every "on" entry must be an r.defineEvent event, otherwise boot fails. The job is no longer fired by the shared job-trigger consumer. JobRunner gains handleCatchUpEvent.

Only the first Authentication-Results header from the top whose authserv-id equals it counts; without an id, without such a header or when its header.from domain differs from the From domain the result is null, and a dmarc result without header.from is unknown. A password IMAP mailbox with a sign-in error now shows Reactivate, which opens the same screen mail-account-reconnect-imap; OAuth mailboxes get the client action reactivate-oauth instead.

- 9638cd4: The OAuth callback only connects a personal mailbox for the account that signed in
  
  InboundOAuthFlow.exchangeCode returns OAuthCodeExchange, an OAuthTokenSet with the required accountAddress of the signed-in provider account. The callback compares it with the mailbox address, ignoring case, and answers 403 mailbox_address_mismatch with a plain-text message and no account when they differ, so nobody can claim another person's address. This applies to personal mailboxes; a shared mailbox (only admins start that flow) is often opened with the admin's own login through delegated access, as with M365 shared mailboxes, so its address is not compared, and a token without access to it shows auth_error on the first sync.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: inbound-mail-foundation
  type: breaking
  title: The OAuth callback only connects a personal mailbox for the account that signed in
  migration: |
    Inbound providers with an oauth block return accountAddress from exchangeCode, taken from the token's email claim or the provider's profile endpoint (for example the userinfo email). There is no default: a provider that cannot name the signed-in address cannot connect mailboxes.
  -->
- 9638cd4: A poison mail no longer blocks the mailbox, quarantined mails get a way back, and attachments are uploaded before the transaction.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: inbound-mail-foundation
  type: improvement
  title: Failing ingests are counted and a poison mail is quarantined after three intervals
  detail: The supervisor counts an ingest failure once per poll interval in the unmanaged table store_mail_ingest_failures, but only when another mail of the account went through in the same poll (for a storage failure another storage write); at three it quarantines the mail with reason ingest_failed and moves the cursor on, before that the batch stops and nothing behind it is skipped. A failure nothing proves to be the mail's (KMS, file storage, the app's storeBody hook, the ingest handler or projection failing for every mail) counts nothing (when every failure of a poll was counted before as a storage or ingest failure, they all keep counting), keeps the cursor and sets the account to degraded with lastError encryption_unavailable, file_storage_unavailable or ingest_unavailable; the next interval retries. An account the supervisor cannot poll because the key store fails while decrypting its address is set to encryption_unavailable too, instead of being skipped silently. A mail that waits for its count clears a shown encryption_unavailable or ingest_unavailable, and file_storage_unavailable once a storage write went through. A requested quarantine retry also runs while a failing mail holds the cursor; during an outage, and when a reload fails because of the provider, the KMS or file storage, the request stays and runs after the recovery. Every quarantined mail also gets a header-only entry (contentState unavailable, contentUnavailableReason quarantined); after a storage failure it goes without the original.
  -->

  feature: inbound-mail-foundation

RejectedInboundMessage may carry rawMime and headers, and an inbound provider's fetch may take filterUnknownMessageIds to skip mails that are already known.

- d24b405: Inbound mail with configurable roles and private personal mailboxes
  
  `createInboundMailFoundationFeature` and `createInboundProviderImapFeature` take `{ userRoles, adminRoles }` (defaults `User` and `TenantAdmin`/`SystemAdmin`); a boot check rejects deviating options. The mail of a personal mailbox (messages, body, attachments, quarantine) is now readable by its owner only, not by admins; admins still see the account metadata and manage shared mailboxes. The owner reactivates a personal IMAP mailbox in the new "My mailboxes" flow. The content-fetched event is version 3 and carries `accountId` and `ownerUserId` (null for older events). `EntityDefinition.attachedFileAccess: "record-only"` keeps the files privileged roles from reading or deleting attached files, and `createDefaultGuard` takes the matching fourth parameter. `SendMailFromAccountContext.dispatch` is query-only. A live list now resyncs on every stream open and an infinity list adopts a refresh that lands during its first load.

  feature: inbound-mail-foundation
  type: breaking
  title: Personal mail is private to its owner, roles are configurable
  detail: Admins no longer read messages, bodies, attachments or quarantine of a personal mailbox; list-accounts still shows them the account without counts. The screens and the IMAP handlers are factories (createMailAccountListScreen, createImapConnectScreen and others) taking the resolved roles instead of constants. The content-fetched event is version 3 with accountId and ownerUserId. createDefaultGuard has a fourth parameter recordOnlyEntityTypes; for those entity types the files privilegedRoles no longer read or delete attached files (shared mailboxes included), only the uploader and readers of the record do. The OAuth connect route answers 403 mail_role_required to callers without a mail role.
  migration: |
    Apps that import mailAccountListScreen, mailAccountEditScreen, mailAccountSenderCheckScreen, myMailAccountListScreen, mailQuarantineScreen, imapConnectScreen or imapReconnectScreen call the matching create*Screen factory with resolveInboundMailRoles(). Apps with their own roles pass { userRoles, adminRoles } to createInboundMailFoundationFeature and the same options to createInboundProviderImapFeature. Callers of createDefaultGuard pass a Set of record-only entity types as fourth argument. Code that read personal mail as an admin must run as the owner; the nullable accountId and ownerUserId on content-fetched events need no action.
  -->

- b638ec7: Add subscription-paddle, a Paddle Billing provider plugin
  
  Checkout via the Paddle.js overlay on a page served by the feature at /billing/paddle-checkout. The Default Payment Link in the Paddle dashboard must point to <APP_BASE_URL>/billing/paddle-checkout; it is the only source, because transactions are created without a checkout url. Create subscription prices in the Paddle catalog with quantity minimum and maximum 1; for one-off packs set the quantity limits on purpose, because the payment event carries quantity and the app has to multiply its credits by it. Also ships customer portal, cancel, resume, batched price lookup, in-app plan switch and tenant binding of checkouts through an HMAC in custom_data.

  title: Add subscription-paddle, a Paddle Billing provider plugin

### Patch Changes

- 9bd6b78: The inbound mail supervisor now passes the system identity as audit user to provider calls when the app's provider context has none. Before, every IMAP poll and watch failed in production because reading the stored mailbox credentials requires an audit identity.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: inbound-mail-foundation
  type: fix
  title: Mail sync no longer fails when reading IMAP credentials
  detail: createInboundMailSupervisor builds its provider context with auditUserId defaulting to the system user. Apps that did not set auditUserId in providerCtx got an internal error on every fetch and watch because the secrets context needs an audit identity. An explicitly set auditUserId is kept.
  -->
- 970a751: The inbound mail supervisor now reads provider credentials in the mail account's tenant scope. Before, under enforced row-level security in production, the worker saw no stored IMAP credentials and set every connected mailbox to auth error.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: inbound-mail-foundation
  type: fix
  title: Mail sync finds the stored IMAP credentials under row-level security
  detail: createInboundMailSupervisor runs outside any request, so secret reads ran without a tenant scope and the application role saw no row in read_tenant_secrets. The supervisor now wraps providerCtx.secrets with tenantScopedSecrets, which the framework exports from internal/row-level-security. inbound-provider-inmemory gains requireCredentialSecretOnFetch so tests can exercise credential reads; a new integration test runs the secrets against an application-role database.
  -->

## 0.392.1

### Patch Changes

- 51fc72c: The "Connect mailbox" form has a required SMTP port field, preset to 587. New mailboxes send over 587 with STARTTLS instead of a fixed port 465, because many hosters (for example Hetzner) block outgoing 465.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: inbound-provider-imap
  type: fix
  title: Mailboxes connect and send over SMTP port 587 with STARTTLS
  detail: The connect form gets a required field "SMTP port", preset to 587, and stores it as smtpPort in the credential document (the schema still accepts any stored port, default now 587). Port 465 uses implicit TLS; every other port uses STARTTLS with requireTLS, so the password is never sent in clear text and the connection fails when the server offers no STARTTLS. The certificate is checked against the host name on the STARTTLS upgrade as well. The SMTP failure texts name the entered port. New key for the field label in all locale packages.
  -->
- 1ded969: A list section with a description and only toolbar actions (for example a create button) shows both in one row: description left, actions right, wrapping below the text on narrow widths. Section headers wrap their actions the same way. The cap cards "view all" link uses the primary link style.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer
  type: fix
  title: List descriptions sit beside the toolbar actions
  detail: A description plus a toolbar with only end content (no search, no facets) renders as one row with the actions on the right, in embedded and full-height lists. Before, a full-height list put the description under the create button. With search or facets the layout is unchanged. Section header actions wrap below the title on narrow widths.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-overview
  type: fix
  title: Cap cards "view all" link uses the primary link style
  detail: The link under the cap cards no longer renders in muted grey; it uses the default link variant like other text links.
  -->

  detail: The new write handler inbound-provider-imap:write:connect-mailbox (TenantAdmin, SystemAdmin, not exposed to the agent, 10 calls per tenant in 10 minutes) checks the IMAP login before the transaction, then creates a shared mail account and stores host, port, user and password in its credential secret in the same transaction. It always connects with implicit TLS (default port 993); there is no plaintext option, and a secure:false in the payload is ignored. A failed check stores nothing and answers with one of four texts: host not reachable or not allowed, login rejected, TLS failed, no connection. It returns WriteResult<{ messageIdHeader }>; failures are typed UnprocessableErrors with the reasons mail_send_not_configured, mail_send_login_rejected, mail_send_server_unreachable, mail_send_rejected and mail_send_invalid_message (i18n keys inboundMail.send.errors.*). A missing, disconnected or someone else's personal mailbox answers not found. There is no fallback to the app sender. New exports: sendMailFromAccount, MAIL_SEND_ERRORS, outboundMailMessageSchema, OutboundMailMessage, OutboundMailSent, MailSendNotConfiguredError, MailSendRejectedError. New keys in all locale packages.

The credential document gains smtpHost and smtpPort (default 465). The provider implements send: it sends over SMTP with From = the mailbox address and display name, then stores the same message in the sent folder (special use \Sent, else Sent, Gesendet or INBOX.Sent); a failed copy is only logged. ### Patch Changes

- 4810041: The inbound mail supervisor reads accounts, sync cursors and seen messages of all tenants in the system scope, so polling no longer finds zero accounts when the app passes the row-level-security enforcing pool.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: inbound-mail-foundation
  type: fix
  title: Mail polling works with the row-level-security enforcing pool
  detail: createInboundMailSupervisor opens its own system scope for the cross-tenant reads and writes of accounts, cursors and seen messages. Before, passing the enforcing pool as db made every poll see no accounts.
  -->
- c639de3: Two new guards: `test-title` flags German or issue-referencing test titles, and `ignore-tag-reason` flags `kumiko-lint-ignore` tags without a real reason. The comment-language guard no longer flags names like "Müller GmbH" or "Zürich".
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement
  title: New test-title and ignore-tag-reason guards, fewer comment-language false positives
  detail: test-title scans test, it and describe titles (including each/skip/only chains) for German text (an umlaut, two German function words, or one unambiguous German word) and issue references. ignore-tag-reason requires a kumiko-lint-ignore reason of at least three words that is not generic. Both start with a baseline of 0 and warn only in repos without a baseline. The comment-language guard now reports a comment only when a lowercase word contains an umlaut, an umlaut appears together with a German function word, or at least two German markers appear, so proper nouns with umlauts pass.
  -->
- 95227c3: The tier-engine resolver reads tier assignments and tenant creation times in system scope, so tenants keep their assigned tier when row-level security is on.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tier-engine
  type: fix
  title: Tier fallback to the default tier under row-level security
  detail: With row-level security enabled (the default since 0.390) the boot preload, the bus-driven reloads and the trial gate of the tier-engine resolver ran on the enforcing pool without a tenant scope, read zero rows and dropped every tenant to the default tier, so toggleable features of paying tenants answered 403 feature_disabled. These reads now run in system scope; no app change is needed.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 8e6d41e: The stream-tenant backfill no longer fails on two membership streams of one (user, tenant) pair, `seedTenantMembership` no longer starts such a second stream, and replicas booting at the same time no longer race on creating `kumiko_es_operations`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant
  type: fix
  title: The stream-tenant backfill archives membership streams a projection replay must not see
  detail: Before the membership projection is rebuilt, the backfill reads the membership lifecycle from the event log and archives two kinds of streams. Streams of a user whose every stream is archived are archived with it, so a rebuild does not bring back memberships of users that no longer exist. When a second stream of a (userId, tenantId) pair was created while another one was still alive, the stream with the newest event stays and the others are archived; a pair that was removed and added again is left alone. Before, the rebuild failed on read_tenant_memberships_unique on every boot and the backfill stayed pending. The archived streams are logged as a warning and returned in membershipStreamsArchived. If a collision still remains, the failure says so and the step runs again on the next boot. Membership rows of archived users disappear from read_tenant_memberships with the rebuild.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant
  type: fix
  title: seedTenantMembership reuses the live membership stream of a pair
  detail: seedTenantMembership looked only at read_tenant_memberships. After the row was lost it created a second stream for the same pair, which made every later rebuild of the projection collide. It now also checks the event log and returns the id of the pair's live stream without writing anything. The seed does not bring the lost row back; only a rebuild of the membership projection does, and nothing triggers one on its own, so until then the user has no membership in that tenant.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Concurrent boots create kumiko_es_operations without a race
  detail: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is not race-safe in Postgres, so replicas booting against a fresh database could fail on pg_type_typname_nsp_index. createEsOperationsTable now takes an advisory lock and checks again before it creates the table.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 8297c01: `schema apply` in the production image heals the framework tables in the runtime's row-level security mode, plus follow-ups from the 0.390 bump: rebuild timestamp drift, scoped live check in `kumiko check`, codemod and upgrade fixes, zod and mailparser security ranges.

  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: schema apply in the production image uses the runtime's row-level security mode
  detail: The app image ships only kumiko/migrations, not kumiko/schema.ts. Without the schema file `schema apply` ran with row-level security "off", so kumiko_events, kumiko_snapshots and kumiko_archived_streams were not healed and the boot of an app in "on" mode (the default) failed with "framework tables without it". Without a schema file apply now uses the same default as runProdApp. RunSchemaCliOptions takes an optional rowLevelSecurity, which wins over the schema file; the scaffolded bin/kumiko.ts passes appConfig.rowLevelSecurity, like bin/main.ts does for runProdApp. Apps that do not set rowLevelSecurity need no change. An app that sets rowLevelSecurity "off" and keeps a hand-written bin/kumiko.ts must pass rowLevelSecurity: "off" to runSchemaCli, otherwise apply enables row-level security on the framework tables and the app's "off" boot check fails.
  -->

  feature: framework

  title: Projection rebuilds no longer report drift on timestamptz columns
  detail: Event payloads keep the microseconds of an instant, the live write stores milliseconds. A rebuild bound the payload's ISO string unchanged and wrote a different value, which the shadow diff reported as column drift. ISO instant strings bound to a timestamptz column are now truncated to milliseconds like Temporal.Instant values.
  -->

An unreachable database still fails the check.

- 5d7dfe1: HandlerContext drops the boot wiring: services, lifecycle and tenants replace the flat members, and hooks receive the HandlerContext.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: HandlerContext without wiring, hooks receive the HandlerContext
  codemod: scripts/codemod/ctx-namespaces.ts
  detail: HandlerContext has 19 members and no longer carries the AppContext wiring. ctx.services holds redis, cacheSync, jobRunner, searchAdapter, entityCache, secrets, kms, files, derivatives, configResolver, configEncryption, rateLimit, effectiveFeatures and masterKeyProvider; every key of an app's extraContext that the framework does not know now lives in ctx.services.extensions (it used to sit flat on the context through a spread, invisible to tsc). ctx.lifecycle holds afterCommit and afterRollback (replacing scheduleAfterCommit and scheduleAfterRollback), signal and runPreSave. ctx.tenants holds config (replacing configFor) and writeTarget (replacing forTenant). ctx.obs gains meter, and the flat log, tracer, _tenantId, systemUser and triggeredBy are gone; read ctx.user.tenantId and ctx.obs.log. JobContext no longer extends the shared wiring fields; it gets services and lifecycle.signal and keeps systemUser, triggeredBy and its job fields. All hooks (preSave, postSave, postSaveBatch, preDelete, postDelete, postDeleteBatch, preQuery, postQuery) and the system hook definitions receive the HandlerContext instead of the AppContext, and the batch hooks run on a real handler context built per flush. AppContext stays the flat boot wiring and declares services as never, so a handler or job context can no longer be passed to a function that takes an AppContext. The context of beforeTransaction no longer exposes ctx.systemDb.outsideTransaction, which was a hole next to the denied ctx.db.outsideTransaction. The member-resolution and pre-transaction contexts also drop the notify factories from ctx.services, and member resolution drops _fileProviderResolver, so neither can rebuild the denied notify or file storage. Helpers that took a structural context with an optional flat member read undefined once a handler context stopped carrying it; their shapes now make that a type error: requireSecretsContext, FileProviderContext (createFileProviderForTenant) and MailTransportContext (createTransportForTenant) take a required secrets key (handlers pass { secrets: ctx.services.secrets, user: ctx.user }), and CreateFileRefContext/UploadFileBytesContext read services.files, so a handler or job context passes straight in. bridgeStub accepts a services option.
  migration: |
    Run kumiko-upgrade --apply; it runs the ctx-namespaces codemod. It rewrites ctx.redis, cacheSync, jobRunner, searchAdapter, entityCache, secrets, kms, files, derivatives, configResolver, effectiveFeatures and the other service members to ctx.services.*, scheduleAfterCommit and scheduleAfterRollback to ctx.lifecycle.afterCommit and afterRollback, signal to ctx.lifecycle.signal, configFor and forTenant to ctx.tenants.config and writeTarget, and hook parameters annotated AppContext to HandlerContext, including context.log to context.obs.log in the hook body. Keys of your extraContext that you read through a cast move to ctx.services.extensions. Listed for manual review: ctx.systemUser, ctx.triggeredBy and ctx._tenantId on a HandlerContext (read ctx.user), a handler or job context passed to a function that takes an AppContext (narrow that parameter to the members it reads), spread literals next to moved members, and a handler or job context passed to a parameter whose structural type reads a moved member (it would read undefined without a type error). Hand-built test contexts take services, lifecycle and tenants from bridgeStub({ services }).
  -->
- f6d230f: Postgres row level security is on by default, system scopes carry a mandatory reason, and the event write path keeps the caller's tenant scope.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: rowLevelSecurity defaults to "on"
  migration: |
    In the app repo, once with the bump: run `kumiko sync-managed --write` (the managed kumiko/schema.ts now reads `export const ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY = appConfig.rowLevelSecurity;`), then `kumiko schema generate` and commit the migration. It contains ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus the policies `kumiko_tenant_isolation` and `kumiko_system_tenant_read` for every tenant table. The schema apply (the migrate init container in production) creates them; there is no manual database step. Without the migration, boot at "on" refuses to start and names the unprotected tables.
    The app's database role must not skip policies; boot refuses it otherwise. Check it as that role with `SELECT rolsuper, rolbypassrls FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = current_user` (both must be false). Callers of createDbConnection without a mode now get "on"; tools that touch no tenant rows (schema baseline/status, the KMS key store) pass "off" explicitly, and the operator commands backfill-pii, waitlist-migrate, project and consumer run on an enforcing connection in system scope, so they work against both modes.
    Way back: set `rowLevelSecurity: "off"` in kumiko.config.ts and run `kumiko schema generate`; the generated migration contains DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and drops the policies. At "off" runProdApp and runWorkerApp log a boot warning.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Boot hooks with a db dependency get a system-scoped db at rowLevelSecurity "on"
  migration: |
    No action unless a hook relied on the unscoped pool. The anonymousAccess factory, enrichAnonymousAccess, the runProdApp `wire` hook and runWorkerApp `wireComponents` now receive a system-scoped db, the same in prod, dev and the test stack, so tenant resolution and boot reads see rows across tenants. Anything the anonymousAccess factory builds keeps that db at request time and therefore reads across tenants for anonymous callers: filter by the resolved tenant yourself. In prod, extraContext factories keep the ambient request scope; the test stack and dev still hand them a system-scoped db, so a service that needs cross-tenant reads at request time must scope itself.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope and systemScopedRunner take a reason
  migration: |
    Call runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope("<why this access spans tenants>", fn) and systemScopedRunner(runner, "<reason>"). An empty or whitespace reason throws InternalError; the scope leak assertion names the reason.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes

  type: breaking

  migration: |

  detail: applyEntityEvent keeps an ambient tenant scope instead of wrapping every write in a system scope. Writes for other tenants go through ctx.systemDb.acknowledgeCrossTenant in an r.systemScope() feature. Replays, rebuilds and global entities still write system scoped.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement
  title: New guard internal-subpath-imports
  detail: Flags kumiko-framework/internal/* imports outside the framework repo, row level security scope helpers from kumiko-testing/helpers in non-test code, and system scope calls without a literal reason.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: jobs
  type: fix
  title: Tenant job run rows are written in the tenant's scope
  detail: With row level security on, the queued, started and finished rows of tenant-visible job runs were rejected by Postgres when the job was dispatched outside a request scope, and the logger only logged the error. The logger now scopes its tenant writes to the job's tenant and logs a rejected write as a missing row-level-security scope instead of a generic write failure.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: composeFeatures no longer warns about its own bundled copies
  detail: Composing the output of a first composeFeatures pass again drops the earlier bundled instances silently; only copies the app supplied itself still warn.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Scoped pool statements pipeline their transaction
  detail: A pool statement under a row level security scope sends BEGIN, the transaction-local scope, the statement and COMMIT pipelined on one reserved connection instead of waiting for each, which cuts its roundtrips roughly in half. The connection returns to the pool only after COMMIT settled.

- 22f9f23: The tenant aggregate is now a global systemStream entity: its stream, read row and search bucket live on SYSTEM_TENANT_ID.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant
  type: breaking
  title: Tenant streams and rows live on the system tenant, seed defaults changed
  detail: Tenants created, renamed or toggled by a SystemAdmin whose session tenant was neither 0001 nor the SYSTEM tenant landed in the event stream, read row and search bucket of that session tenant, so later updates could not find them. The tenant entity is now declared systemStream with tenancy global, so every writer (create, update, enable and disable, request and cancel destruction, the destroy job stages) addresses the stream on SYSTEM_TENANT_ID. seedTenant, seedUser, seedAdmin and seedAdminGuarded default to createSystemUser(SYSTEM_TENANT_ID) and write the tenant to SYSTEM whatever tenant an explicit by acts from; managed-pages and compliance-profiles seeds default to createSystemUser(tenantId). Existing memberships written by an admin of another tenant sit on that admin's stream while read_tenant_memberships.tenant_id carries the member tenant; after the backfill streamTenantId equals tenantId for them. New export backfillTenantStreamTenants from the tenant feature, the boot step runStreamTenantBackfillOnBoot in server-runtime, EsOperationType gains "stream-migration", built on the generic backfillAggregateStreamTenants in shared (backfillUserStreamTenants keeps its signature).
  migration: |
    Nothing to run: runProdApp (api, all-in-one) and runWorkerApp search for legacy tenant, membership and user streams on every boot, before the boot seeds respectively before the worker starts, and fix what they find. A boot with nothing left reads only events of other tenants than SYSTEM (plus the membership events) and does no rebuild or reindex. It merges split tenant streams onto SYSTEM_TENANT_ID, moves each membership stream to the tenantId of its payload, moves legacy user streams, removes stale search documents from the old buckets, and where streams moved rebuilds tenant:projection:tenant-entity, tenant:projection:tenant-membership-entity and user:projection:user-entity and reindexes the tenant and user search indexes. Legacy streams written by old pods during a rolling deploy are fixed on the next boot. A row in kumiko_es_operations (stream-tenant-backfill:<user|tenant>:derived-pending) marks a run in progress so that a crash after the moves still gets its rebuild and reindex. Parallel boots are serialized by a Postgres advisory lock; failures are logged (aggregateId, step, error) and retried on the next boot. A process without a search adapter leaves the work to one that has it. Library users can call backfillTenantStreamTenants or backfillUserStreamTenantsWithDerivedState directly. Code that read tenant streams with loadAggregate(db, tenantId, "tenant") or appended tenant events with the tenant id as stream tenant must use SYSTEM_TENANT_ID. Consumer workarounds that wrote tenant streams under a SystemAdmin `by` (for example an executor update with TestUsers.systemAdmin) are no longer needed, because the stream is always SYSTEM. Seeds that relied on the old by default (TestUsers.systemAdmin) now get the system user as audit actor. Apps without a search backend set `search: "none"` on runProdApp and runWorkerApp, otherwise the stream-tenant backfill stays deferred in every process that has no search adapter.
  -->

- 6d20414: Row level security at runtime: connections set the tenant or system scope in every transaction, one rowLevelSecurity value in kumiko.config.ts drives schema tooling and boot, and the test stack and the dev server run with it on.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Connections set the row level security scope in every transaction
  detail: createDbConnection takes rowLevelSecurity "off" or "on" (default "off", the connection is unchanged). With "on", every statement and transaction sets kumiko.tenant_id and kumiko.scope transaction-locally from the ambient scope. TenantDb sets its tenant, and the system scope for system-mode TenantDbs, global tables and a granted unsafeRaw. Dispatch sets the user's tenant per command, or the system scope for a system-scoped handler. Event store reads and writes use the stream's tenant. Jobs, the event dispatcher, member resolution, migrations, boot seeds, retention, reindex, blind-index cleanup, the PII backfill, projection apply, auth providers and the tenant lifecycle check run in system scope. A statement without a scope sees no tenant rows. The functions that set a scope (runInRowLevelSecurityScope, runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope, tenantRowLevelSecurityScope, systemScopedRunner) are not part of the public db subpath; framework packages import them from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/internal/row-level-security, which no guard closes to apps yet. App code reaches the system scope through a system-scoped handler, a job or a granted unsafeRaw.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: One rowLevelSecurity value in kumiko.config.ts for schema tooling and runners
  detail: AppConfig.rowLevelSecurity ("off" by default) is exported by the managed kumiko/schema.ts as ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY. kumiko-schema generate and validate render and check the policies from it, and apply opens its connection in that mode; the CLI has no flag of its own. The API, worker and all-in-one entrypoints take the same option and refuse a context whose connection runs in another mode. unsafePushTables with "on" reads the catalog first and runs no lock and no DDL for a table that already has ENABLE, FORCE and both kumiko policies.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Projection rebuilds run in system scope under row level security
  detail: The rebuild transaction no longer turns row_security off, so a rebuild works as a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS table owner under FORCE. Before the first guard read it locks the live table in SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE mode, which blocks policy DDL and a second rebuild of the same table, and reads the catalog. When row level security is enabled, kumiko_tenant_isolation must exist as a PERMISSIVE policy for ALL commands and PUBLIC and no RESTRICTIVE policy may exist; otherwise the rebuild fails with the table and its policies and leaves the live table untouched. Other permissive policies carry over to the swapped-in table. Multi-stream rebuilds follow the same rule.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: runProdApp checks the row level security state at boot
  detail: RunProdAppOptions.rowLevelSecurity ("off" by default) sets the mode of every connection; the scaffolded server entry passes appConfig.rowLevelSecurity. With "on", boot fails when the database role has SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS, because Postgres then skips every policy, and when a table with tenant_id lacks ENABLE, FORCE or one of the two kumiko policies; the message lists the tables. With "off", boot fails while any table still has row level security enabled and points to the DISABLE migration that kumiko-schema generate writes.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: user-data-rights
  type: fix
  title: User data export and forget cleanup run in system scope
  detail: runUserExport and runForgetCleanup walk every tenant of a user, so they enter the system scope themselves instead of depending on the caller's scope. A direct call outside a job no longer exports or erases nothing under row level security "on".
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: testing
  type: breaking
  title: The test stack runs with row level security on as role kumiko_app
  detail: setupTestStack creates the role kumiko_app (LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS, password taken from TEST_DATABASE_URL) once, makes it owner of the test database and opens every pool as that role with rowLevelSecurity "on"; template databases are built the same way. stack.db runs in system scope and sees every tenant's rows as before. The new stack.unscopedDb is the enforced pool the services use, on which a statement without a scope sees no tenant rows. rowLevelSecurity: "off" in the stack options restores the superuser stack without policies. createTestDb takes applicationRole: true for the same setup.
  migration: App code that reads or writes tenant tables through a raw connection outside a request, a job or a TenantDb now sees no rows in integration tests. Test code that calls such a path directly runs it inside runInSystemRowLevelSecurityScope or runInRowLevelSecurityScope(tenantRowLevelSecurityScope(tenantId), ...) from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/helpers. Production code works through a TenantDb for the tenant, a job, a system-scoped handler or a granted unsafeRaw. Tests that need superuser rights on stack.db, such as CREATE EXTENSION, CREATE ROLE or event triggers, open their own connection from TEST_DATABASE_URL or use createTestDb(). Manual migration, there is no codemod.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: breaking
  title: The dev server runs with row level security on
  detail: runDevApp and createKumikoServer default to rowLevelSecurity "on" and run the dev stack as kumiko_app. On boot against a persistent dev database, the stack creates the role and transfers ownership of the database and of the public schema's tables, views and sequences to kumiko_app. The database user in DATABASE_URL needs the right to create roles, which the superuser of a local Postgres has. Code that reads tenant tables through a raw connection without a scope sees no rows in development; the boot does not detect this. runSchemaApply takes rowLevelSecurity, and the managed kumiko/schema.ts exports ROW_LEVEL_SECURITY from appConfig; the managed file updates on the next sync.
  migration: Pass rowLevelSecurity: "off" to runDevApp while fixing code paths without tenant context; the dev database keeps kumiko_app as owner. A server entry written by an older scaffold passes appConfig.rowLevelSecurity to runProdApp by hand once the app turns row level security on. Manual migration, there is no codemod.
  -->

## 0.389.0

### Minor Changes

- 47ba075: Password reset and signup accept an optional `returnTo` path that is carried through the mailed link and the web screens.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: improvement
  title: Optional returnTo for password reset and signup
  detail: Password reset and signup accept an optional returnTo path. A safe value (same-origin path, no dot segments) is appended to the mailed link as a query parameter, the reset and signup-complete screens follow it, and the login screen forwards its next to the forgot-password and signup links. Invalid values are dropped silently and never block the mail. isSafeReturnPath and readReturnToFromSearch are exported from the web barrel. isSafeNextPath now uses the same check, so a next with a dot segment such as "/a/../b" is no longer followed.
  -->
- c16fa0c: `bundledLists` sets one DataTable `table` block for every list screen and relatedList section of the bundled features.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: bundledLists sets one table block for every bundled list
  detail: composeFeatures takes bundledLists with a table block and an optional pinFirstColumn flag. The block is mixed into every entityList, projectionList and relatedList section of the bundled features, the foundation features user and tenant as well as the features an app mounts from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features, before the boot validator runs. A key the screen sets itself wins, export is left out on relatedList sections, and pinFirstColumn pins the first visible column left where no column is pinned yet. grouping and totals are rejected in the shared block. App screens stay untouched. Features opt in with the new registrar method r.adoptsBundledLists(), which every bundled feature with lists calls and which feature packages such as Enterprise can call for their own lists; app features never do. No migration for apps. The option lives in AppConfig.bundledLists for the managed kumiko/schema.ts and in the run options of runProdApp, runDevApp and runWorkerApp, so kumiko check and the running app see the same screens.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: validateBundledListsOptions and the BundledListsOptions type
  detail: BundledListsOptions is exported from the types package and the engine barrel. validateBundledListsOptions rejects unknown keys, grouping, totals and pinFirstColumn without table.pinning with a message that names the key, and checks the remaining keys like a screen's own table block.

  <!-- kumiko-changes

- ac00e8a: List screens get a `table` block: remembered filter, search and sort per user, a reset-all button, a column picker with reordering, and a comfortable or compact row density.

Columns accept hidden: true. Remembered state lives in sessionStorage per tenant and user and is cleared on logout or identity change.

It only compared the status and treated a deleted user with status `active` as active; use `isPrincipalRowBlocked(row)` from the `user` export for the login block, or `isPrincipalBlocked` from `user` where a plain status comparison is meant.

- 2602c62: A config key's `validate` function can read the cascade of any registered key through `ctx.readCascade(qualifiedKey)`, for example to check the operator default before accepting a tenant value.

- 2602c62: `legalContentSeed(source, { folder })` and `seedLegalContentFromJson(db, blocks, { folder })` put the seeded text blocks into a content-tree folder. A re-seed without a folder option now keeps the folder an existing block already has, instead of resetting it to the root on every boot. `seedTextBlock` with `ifExists: "update"` now keeps an existing folder whenever `folder` is omitted; clearing it needs an explicit `folder: null`.
