## 0.376.0

### Minor Changes

- 05ba6c5: runDevApp and runWorkerApp understand the declarative boot options of runProdApp, and the default mail resolver stops reaching users outside the notifying tenant.
  
  `runDevApp` takes `mail`, `fileStorage`, `kmsMode`, `billing`, `seeds` (shortcuts plus free seeds that get the test stack), `demoMode`, `envSchema` and `featureToggles`; `runWorkerApp` takes `mail`, `fileStorage`, `kmsMode`, `billing`, `featureToggles` and `envSchema` and understands every `KUMIKO_DRY_RUN_ENV` mode. All of them resolve through the same functions as `runProdApp`. `featureToggles: true` mounts feature-toggles and layers the global operator switches over the tier resolver; `composeSaasStack({ featureToggles: true })` expects it. `runProdApp` seeds and `extraContext` factories receive `masterKeyProvider` and `configEncryption`; `appOverrides` overrides tenant-model, branding and seo defaults.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: breaking
  title: effectiveFeatures is gone from runProdApp, runDevApp and runWorkerApp
  detail: The effectiveFeatures option of the boot functions is removed. Global operator switches come from the featureToggles option, tier gating from the tier-engine feature, which the boot functions wire themselves.
  migration: Replace a hand-built effectiveFeatures resolver with featureToggles true (global switches) and mount createTierEngineFeature for tier gating. A custom resolver that did neither has no replacement on the boot functions; wire it through createKumikoServer or setupTestStack in tests. The boot functions now abort when the option is still passed, because an ignored option would drop an operator kill-switch silently; the same goes for a feature-toggles feature in features without the featureToggles option, or with it set (the option mounts the feature).
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: breaking
  title: The default mail resolver only reaches members of the notifying tenant
  detail: The default resolveEmail of the mail boot option returns an address for a notification from a tenant other than the system tenant only if the user is a member of that tenant or holds the SystemAdmin role in the stored user row. Everyone else resolves to null and the mail is skipped. The new option mail.recipientScope takes "membership" (default) or "any", which restores the old behaviour of reaching every user. EmailChannelOptions resolveEmail now receives the tenant database as TenantDb instead of unknown.
  migration: Apps that notify users outside the notifying tenant on purpose, for example merchants reached from a SystemAdmin context, set mail recipientScope to "any" or keep their own resolveEmail. Apps whose notifications go to members of the active tenant need no change. Known consumers on the default: offlot-app (main.ts) reaches merchants and SystemAdmins across tenants and needs recipientScope any; publicstatus (main.ts), show-pony, solon (main.ts) and kumiko-studio (main.ts) take the default, which fits notifications to members of the active tenant. money-horse and phronexsis keep their own resolveEmail. Per-app resolvers that only copied the membership check can be deleted. A custom resolveEmail that cast ctx.db can drop the cast.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: channel-email
  type: improvement
  title: resolveEmail receives a typed tenant database
  detail: The context of EmailChannelOptions resolveEmail types db as TenantDb, so resolvers read tables without a cast.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: runDevApp and runWorkerApp take the declarative boot options
  detail: mail, fileStorage, kmsMode, billing, seeds, demoMode, envSchema and featureToggles work in runDevApp, and mail, fileStorage, kmsMode, billing, featureToggles and envSchema in runWorkerApp, through the same resolve functions as runProdApp. The worker honours KUMIKO_DRY_RUN_ENV with an env schema. A stack that sets runSingleInstance false only warns when no worker mounts the features.
  migration: RunDevAppOptions.seeds is now `readonly SeedFn[] | RunDevAppSeedsConfig`. Code that spreads `seeds` from an object typed as RunDevAppOptions no longer type-checks; declare that object with `satisfies RunDevAppOptions` so the array type survives, or build the seed list separately. An app that lists createFeatureTogglesFeature() in the features passed to runDevApp or runProdApp removes it there and sets `featureToggles: true`.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: featureToggles, appOverrides and secrets in boot deps
  detail: featureToggles true mounts feature-toggles and layers the global switches over the tier resolver in runProdApp, runDevApp and runWorkerApp. appOverrides sets tenant-model, branding and seo defaults. masterKeyProvider and configEncryption reach extraContext factories, system wiring and seed functions, so an app no longer resolves its KEK a second time.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: Boot errors for removed and half-wired feature toggles
  detail: runProdApp, runDevApp and runWorkerApp abort when the removed effectiveFeatures option is still passed, and when feature-toggles sits in features without the featureToggles option. runWorkerApp now enforces a stack that expects featureToggles, so a worker cannot keep running jobs and event handlers of features an operator switched off.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: Named S3 provider names are validated at boot
  detail: fileStorage.providers refuses the names s3-env, s3 and inmemory, which the bundled providers register, and a name listed twice. A tenant admin can still select any mounted provider through the file-foundation provider config, so name a provider only if every tenant may use its bucket.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime

- 5274ebc: Host routing takes an app resolver, redirects and a per-host anonymous query allowlist; legal pages pass `alternates` to the layout; account-security constants have a client-safe subpath.
  
  `createHostRoutingFeature` and `createHostDispatch` accept `tenantBy: (host, db) => TenantId | null` next to `"host"` and `"path"`. The resolver maps every host that is neither the apex nor a fixed host (profile subdomains, custom domains) to a tenant; the result must still be an enabled, active tenant, and null answers 404 on the page side and `tenant_required` on the API side. `tenantPathPrefix` is now optional in host and resolver mode and serves `<prefix>/<key>` on the apex next to the host tenants. `redirects: [{ from, to, host?, status? }]` are checked before any host classification; `to` is a configured same-origin path or https URL, only the matched path remainder and the query string are appended. `apexAnonymousQueryAllowlist: { [apexHost]: [queryType] }` limits which `/api/query` and `/api/stream` types get the `apexAnonymousTenantId` anchor on that host; without an entry the behavior is unchanged. `example.com` and `www.example.com` share one entry, and the check runs on the decoded route path (`/api/%71uery` and a trailing slash are covered). In `tenantBy: "path"` mode the client names its tenant and would bypass the allowlist, so `apexAnonymousQueryAllowlist` together with `tenantBy: "path"` now throws at boot (breaking for apps that combine them). `createHostTenantIdResolver(options, db)` returns a `host => TenantId | null` function for managed-pages' `resolveApexTenant`.
  
  `createLegalPagesLayout` hands `alternates` (locale to path of the same page) as the second argument to `headerHtml` and `footerHtml`, and the legal-pages routes now supply it for slugs served in more than one language. `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/account-security/constants` exports the feature id, screen id, screen QN, nav label and the new `ACCOUNT_SECURITY_SCREEN_TITLE_KEY` without server imports.

Existing "host" and "path" configs behave as before, except that apexAnonymousQueryAllowlist with tenantBy "path" is rejected at boot.
  -->

## 0.374.0

### Minor Changes

- de5d674: clientAction row actions backed by a client registry
  
  A row action with `kind: "clientAction"` runs a function from a client bundle instead of a write handler. The schema carries `action: "<feature>:<kebab>"`; a client feature registers the function under `ClientFeatureDefinition.clientActions` (merged like `columnRenderers`, last wins with a warning). The handler gets the payload (default `{ id: row.id }`, or the `payload` extractor) and returns `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, message }`. Success shows a toast (`successMessage`, default "Done.") and refetches, a failure shows an error toast, and a throw or an unregistered name shows a generic one and logs the name. `confirm`, `confirmLabel`, `style: "danger"`, `visible`, `icon` and `display` work as on a write handler; `redirect` and `rowClick` do not exist. Toolbar actions do not take it. Boot rejects a name that is not `<feature>:<kebab>`.
  
  auth-email-password registers `auth-email-password:request-password-reset` and `auth-email-password:request-email-verification`, both taking `{ email }`.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: clientAction row actions
  detail: RowAction gains kind "clientAction" with a client-registered handler name; boot rejects a name that is not <feature>:<kebab>, and the surface keys include its confirm, confirmLabel and successMessage.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer
  type: improvement
  title: Client action registry for row actions
  detail: ClientActionsProvider, ActionNoticeProvider and runClientAction execute clientAction row actions on list, related list and record actions, with confirm, toast feedback and refetch.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer-web
  type: improvement
  title: ClientFeatureDefinition.clientActions
  detail: Client features register clientAction handlers; createKumikoApp merges them and shows their outcome as toasts.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: improvement
  title: Client actions for password reset and email verification
  detail: emailPasswordClient registers auth-email-password:request-password-reset and auth-email-password:request-email-verification for clientAction row actions.
  -->
- 926e08e: Dashboards bound to a record, with header actions, auto refresh and relative times
  
  `DashboardScreenDefinition.record: { param, payloadKey?, query?, titleField? }` ties a dashboard to one record via a URL search param. The id is merged into every panel and `visibleWhen` gate query after `filter`/`timeRange` and before a panel's own `params`; screen-kind panels get none. Without the param the dashboard shows a hint (`kumiko.dashboard.record.missing`) and runs no query. `record.query` loads the record row for the page title (`titleField`), the actions and `refresh.field`.
  
  `actions` puts writeHandler, navigate and clientAction actions in the dashboard header, running on the record row (or `{ id, [payloadKey]: id }` without `record.query`). After a success the record and all panels refetch. The header bar is the shared `HeaderActionsBar` component also used by projectionDetail. Boot rejects actions without `record`, drawer actions, `rowClick` and `redirect`.
  
  `refresh: { seconds } | { field }` polls the record and all panels, never faster than 5 s (`DASHBOARD_MIN_REFRESH_SECONDS`): boot rejects `seconds` below it, a `field` value is clamped at runtime. A running refetch is never stacked and polling stops on unmount.
  
  `valueFormat: { kind: "relativeTime" }` on stat panels and `{ kind: "relativeTime", atMs }` as a text param render epoch ms via `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` in the user locale ("5 minutes ago", "in 30 seconds") and keep ticking while mounted.
  
  fillAction is only allowed on text, number, decimal and bigInt fields and rejected on password, sensitive and writeOnly ones; an actionForm `load` never fills those fields from the loaded record. The email clientActions answer a 429 with the new `auth.errors.tooManyRequests` instead of the login-specific rate-limit text.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Dashboard record binding, header actions, refresh and relative time
  detail: Dashboards take record, actions and refresh; stat panels and text params gain a relativeTime format; the surface keys include kumiko.dashboard.record.missing.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: DashboardChartPanel.valueFormat only takes the currency format
  detail: DashboardValueFormat is now a union of DashboardCurrencyFormat and DashboardRelativeTimeFormat. Stat panels take both, chart panels only the currency one, and boot rejects relativeTime on a chart.
  migration: A chart panel that declares valueFormat keeps working with { kind: "currency", currency }. Code that types a chart's valueFormat as DashboardValueFormat should use DashboardCurrencyFormat instead; relativeTime on a chart was never meaningful and now fails boot.
  -->
- 1b710f1: pagedListSchema and pageRows for in-memory projectionList queries, tenant-caps:list pages by offset
  
  `pagedListSchema(sortableFields)` is the query schema for a projectionList whose rows are merged in memory: `limit`, `offset`, `search`, `sort` (enum of the sortable fields), `sortDirection` and `totalCount`. `pageRows(rows, request, { searchFields, defaultSort })` searches case-insensitively, sorts (missing values last, ties by `id`), slices by `offset` and `limit`, and returns a `CursorResult` with `nextCursor: null` and `total` only when `totalCount` is set.
  
  `cap-overview:query:tenant-caps:list` now uses them. The projectionList pager sends `offset` and never a cursor, so every page used to show page 1. The query no longer pages by `cursor`: a caller that still sends one gets a 400 validation error instead of page 1 (`pagedListSchema` rejects `cursor`). An unknown `sort` is rejected by the schema.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: pagedListSchema and pageRows for in-memory list queries
  detail: pagedListSchema(sortableFields) and pageRows(rows, request, { searchFields, defaultSort }) cover search, sort (missing values last, ties by id), offset paging and an optional total for projectionList queries over merged rows. PagedListRequest and PagedListRowValue are exported; nextCursor is always null.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-overview
  type: breaking
  title: tenant-caps:list pages by offset and rejects cursor
  detail: The cap overview list showed page 1 on every page because the pager sends offset and the query only read cursor. tenant-caps:list now takes offset like the pager; a cursor in the payload is rejected with a 400 validation error and sort is an enum of the sortable fields. The unused cap-overview.errors.invalidCursor and sortFieldUnsupported keys are gone.
  migration: Callers of cap-overview:query:tenant-caps:list must send offset instead of cursor, and only a sortable field name as sort. Apps that override the removed i18n keys cap-overview.errors.invalidCursor or cap-overview.errors.sortFieldUnsupported can delete them. No caller in the kumiko-enterprise, kumiko-platform, kumiko-studio or app repos sends a cursor or defines these keys.
  -->

## 0.372.0

### Minor Changes

- 16ab9fe: Queued delivery jobs carry the recipient address sealed
  
  `delivery.render` and `delivery.send` job payloads sit in Redis and the job-run table. With a master key configured, the recipient address now travels as `sealedAddress` (encrypted per tenant) and is opened only right before `channel.send`. Without a master key the payload keeps the plaintext `address` and boot logs one warning. Jobs queued before the upgrade keep their plaintext address and still send.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: breaking
  title: Queued delivery jobs carry the recipient address sealed
  detail: createDeliveryService takes an addressCipher; the boot wiring passes the master-key cipher, so delivery.render and delivery.send payloads hold sealedAddress instead of address. Workers open it through ctx.configEncryption.
  migration: Roll out worker and web together with the same KUMIKO_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY_V<n>; a worker without the master key fails sealed jobs with send_failed. Code that calls createDeliveryService itself passes addressCipher to get sealed payloads.
  -->
- 7c04d2a: App unsubscribe pages can wear the tenant's mail look
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: createUnsubscribePageChromeReader gives app routes the tenant branding for unsubscribe pages
  detail: The JSDoc of renderUnsubscribeResultPage pointed to a chrome read that only works for SystemAdmin, so app routes for legacy unsubscribe links rendered without branding. The new `createUnsubscribePageChromeReader({ dispatchSystemQuery })` returns `(tenantId, locale) => MailChrome | null`, failing soft to null. Build it once in the `wire` hook, whose deps now also carry `dispatchSystemQuery` (runProdApp, runWorkerApp.wireComponents, createKumikoServer), and call it with a tenant the route resolved itself, for example from the Host, never with a tenantId from the query string or body. The chrome query itself stays SystemAdmin-only; anonymous `/api/query` callers are still rejected for every tenant.
  -->
- 236858e: `executor.detail()` and `executor.list()` return the entity's row type
  
  `createEntityExecutor(name, entity)` and `createEventStoreExecutor(table, entity, options)` now return `EventStoreExecutor<EntityRow<E>>`. `detail` resolves to `EntityRow<E> | null` and `list` to `CursorResult<EntityRow<E>>`, so `row.title` needs no cast or schema parse. `EntityRow<E>` is exported from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db` and follows what the executor returns at runtime: money is one `{ amount, currency, amountScaled, amountMinor }` key, a located timestamp one `{ at, tz, utc }` key, `date` is a `Temporal.PlainDate`, `timestamp` and `insertedAt` are `Temporal.Instant`, soft-delete keys are required only when `softDelete` is the literal `true`, and bigInt and jsonb stay `unknown`. A wide `fields` map falls back to `Record<string, unknown>`. Create and update payloads stay untyped, and a typed executor is still assignable to the untyped `EventStoreExecutor`.
  
  `createBooleanField` is now typed as non-null (`default: boolean`), matching what it stores.
  
  Breaking: a `row as T` cast whose target the row type no longer overlaps becomes a compile error, and casts that still compile but are now redundant can go. Run the codemod first, then fix what it lists as manual.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: executor.detail() and executor.list() return EntityRow<E>, derived from the entity definition
  detail: Rows of createEntityExecutor / createEventStoreExecutor are typed per entity; wide entities keep Record<string, unknown>. createBooleanField is typed non-null. UserMfaRow in the bundled auth-mfa feature now declares enabledAt and lastUsedAt as Temporal.Instant, which is what the row always held.
  migration: Remove the `row as T` casts on executor.detail() / executor.list() results with `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply` (codemod remove-engine-payload-casts). Casts to a type the row does not satisfy stay and are listed as manual; replace them with a field-level check or a narrower type.
  codemod: scripts/codemod/remove-engine-payload-casts.ts
  manualAfterCodemod: true
  -->
- 27b759f: Orphaned upload bytes are swept
  
  Bytes written by `POST /files`, `createFileRefFromBytes`, `uploadFileBytesBeforeTransaction` and the seed `createFileRef` are recorded in the new `store_file_upload_ledger` table before they reach storage. The commit that creates the fileRef row removes the ledger row in its own transaction. The new hourly `files:job:sweep-orphaned-uploads` job deletes the bytes (original and derivatives) of uploads still unclaimed after `uploadSweepGraceHours` (default 24, minimum 1; option of `createFilesFeature`). A commit that arrives after its upload was swept fails with `upload expired`. Plain `files.ref(key).write()` stays untracked and is never swept.
  
  `FileContext` gains `writeUploadBytes` and `forgetUploadBytes`, `FileProviderResolver` may carry `uploadLedgerFor`, and `TenantDb.deleteMany` now returns the number of deleted rows. Build a tenant's `FileContext` with `createTenantFileContext(resolver, tenantId)` so it carries the resolver's ledger.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: files
  type: breaking
  title: Orphaned upload bytes are swept through a new upload ledger
  detail: The files feature registers the store_file_upload_ledger table and an hourly sweep job. FileContext has the new methods writeUploadBytes and forgetUploadBytes, which the four upload paths use; a custom FileContext or resolver must provide the ledger (withUploadLedger wraps a resolver). TenantDb.deleteMany resolves to the number of deleted rows instead of void. A fileRef commit whose ledger row was already swept throws InternalError "upload expired".
  migration: Generate and apply a migration with `kumiko-schema generate` — uploads fail without the new store_file_upload_ledger table
  -->

Preview, the sample values bar and send-test therefore show German examples for a German template. Example values of other types (link, number, enum-like text values) stay as declared; put the explanation of such a value into the variable's label. Apps: register `templateVariable.text({ example: "<app>:mail.example.x" })` and add the key with de, en and es via `r.translations`.
  -->

## 0.371.0

### Minor Changes

- 5a822b2: Consumer findings from the second rollout wave
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: Default mail resolveEmail finds users of any tenant
  detail: The default resolveEmail of the mail boot option loads the user by id only. Rows in read_users carry the system tenant, so the former tenantId filter returned null for every real tenant.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: extraContext factories see the boot env, billing hook and new exports
  detail: The merged env, including the defaults of declarative boot options such as FILE_STORAGE_PROVIDER from fileStorage, is passed to extraContext factories as env. resolveBillingOption, parseRunMode, HostDispatchFn, buildDemoModeRoute and withDemoReadOnlyFetch are exported from the package index. The billing boot option accepts afterSync.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: file-provider-s3
  type: improvement
  title: S3 endpoint over http outside production
  detail: s3EndpointSchema rejects http on non-loopback hosts only when NODE_ENV=production, so compose hostnames such as minio work in smoke setups.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-foundation
  type: improvement
  title: Boot warning when anonymous routes run without anonymousAccess
  detail: A boot warning names anonymousAccess when host-routing, managed-pages or legal-pages is mounted without it; anonymous requests get no tenant until the option is set.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: billing-foundation
  type: improvement
  title: Billing webhook sync exposes afterSync
  detail: The billing webhook sync calls afterSync({ tenantId, tier, changed, event }) after every webhook, with changed false when the tier stayed the same.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: Unsubscribe endpoint answers form posts with an HTML page
  detail: POST on the delivery unsubscribe route returns an HTML confirmation page for a form post and JSON for a bare POST. The behavior is unchanged; this only documents it.
  migration: Clients that post the unsubscribe form expect HTML, API clients that post without a form content type expect JSON. No code change is needed.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Dry-run env table and boot check respect required overrides and the fileStorage default
  detail: The env table of KUMIKO_DRY_RUN_ENV=boot shows a variable as required when the app schema overlays required() on an optional field, and the error says required. The schema-cli boot check applies runProdApp's fileStorage default instead of demanding FILE_STORAGE_PROVIDER.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: testing
  type: improvement
  title: Scaffold test:dom passes without test files
  detail: The scaffold sets test:dom to pass without test files and adds the devDependencies @testing-library/react, @testing-library/dom and @happy-dom/global-registrator.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: guards
  type: improvement
  title: Pre-push shim stops at the repo boundary, nearest kumiko.json wins, process.env guard covers bin
  detail: The pre-push shim searches upward only through ancestors up to the git root and fails with a message when nothing is found. findLocalRepo prefers the nearest kumiko.json over the git root. guard-no-direct-process-env scans bin/**/*.ts including bin/ops.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: improvement
  title: composeGdprStack access, composePagesStack terms, migrate-step project name
  detail: composeGdprStack({ access }) is passed to compliance-profiles and composeOpsStack({ access }) to delivery as their handler roles. composePagesStack({ terms }) is passed to legal-pages. DevHostDispatch and DevHostDispatchResult are exported. The migrate-step.sh template and the managed pre-push template follow the show-pony version, with the compose project name taken from docker compose config.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cli
  type: improvement
  title: kumiko codemod lists and runs codemods
  detail: kumiko codemod lists the codemods without a name. kumiko codemod <name> runs one against the current directory as a dry run and applies it with --write.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer
  type: improvement
  title: Missing-screen page spaces title and hint like other cards
  detail: The page-not-available card renders title and hint through the Card title and subtitle slots.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: locale-de
  type: improvement
  title: errors.demoReadOnly translated
  detail: The read-only demo error has German copy in the informal and formal catalogs.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: locale-es
  type: improvement
  title: errors.demoReadOnly translated
  detail: The read-only demo error has Spanish copy.

## 0.370.0

### Minor Changes

- a02e354: New bundled feature account-security
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: account-security
  type: improvement
  title: createAccountSecurityFeature bundles the self-service screen for MFA and own sessions
  detail: createAccountSecurityFeature({ nav?, access? }) registers account-security:screen:account-security, a dashboard that embeds the auth-mfa enable, regenerate and disable screens and the sessions list of the signed-in user. It owns no handlers; mount it next to auth-mfa and sessions, or let composeAuthStack({ mfa }) mount it. Without nav the screen is dormant (no sidebar entry); nav takes { order?, parent? } with order 90 by default. access defaults to every signed-in user. Apps with a local copy of this screen replace it with the bundled feature.
  -->
- a02e354: New bundled feature host-routing
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: host-routing
  type: improvement
  title: createHostRoutingFeature and createHostDispatch route tenants by host or path
  detail: One HostRoutingOptions object ({ tenantBy: "host" } or { tenantBy: "path", tenantPathPrefix }, plus baseDomain, apex, tenant, unknownTenant?, hosts?, locales?) drives both halves. createHostRoutingFeature registers an authoritative Host-header tenant resolver in host mode and, in both modes, an existence check that admits only enabled, active tenants. apexAnonymousTenantId gives anonymous apex calls a tenant (e.g. SYSTEM_TENANT_ID); without it the apex answers tenant_required. createHostDispatch is a runProdApp hostDispatch: HTML file and optional CSP per surface (without csp the runProdApp default applies), a 301 from the default-locale prefix to the unprefixed path, and 404 for unknown tenants and hosts. toDevHostDispatch(dispatch, { entries, staticDir }) from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-dev-server plugs the same decision into the dev server. Apps with their own routing feature and hostDispatch move to these; app-specific redirects or custom domains wrap the dispatch function.
  -->
- 79a0aa6: Stacks name the runProdApp option they need, plus auth, SaaS and security stacks
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: runProdApp names the stack and the boot option it is missing
  detail: Features returned by the compose*Stack helpers carry bootRequires ({ stack, options }), a new optional FeatureDefinition field; BootOptionName and StackBootRequirement are exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine. runProdApp checks them before it wires the boot options and fails with "[runProdApp] stacks in `features` need boot options that are not set:" followed by one line per gap, for example "composeSaasStack needs the boot option `billing`: set billing: { stripe: { priceToTier }, defaultTier }". composeMailStack and composeUserDataRightsStack need mail (or a mounted channel-email), composeFileStack without providers needs fileStorage (or a mounted file provider), composeGdprStack and composeSecurityStack need kmsMode (or kms / allowPlaintextPii), composeSecurityStack also fails with rateLimit: false, composeSaasStack with billing "stripe" needs billing (or a mounted subscription provider). composeFileStack takes providers as optional now. The renderer, pages, ops and identity stacks need no option. resolveBillingOption is exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-server-runtime/boot-options/billing for tests that mount the billing wiring on a test stack.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: improvement
  title: composeAuthStack, composeSaasStack and composeSecurityStack
  detail: composeAuthStack({ sessions?, mfa?, accountSecurity? }) mounts auth-foundation and sessions, with mfa also auth-mfa and account-security; the password login still comes from the auth option or composeFeatures. composeSaasStack({ billing: "stripe" | "mollie", tiers, caps?, waitlist?, billingFoundation? }) mounts billing-foundation and tier-engine, cap-counter plus cap-overview with caps, waitlist with waitlist. With "stripe" the runProdApp billing option mounts subscription-stripe and the tier-sync webhook route; with "mollie" the stack mounts subscription-mollie from the mollie options and the app adds the webhook route. composeSecurityStack({ includeSessions? }) mounts sessions, crypto-shredding, rate-limiting and audit. composeGdprStack({ selfService: { userDataRights? } }) adds sessions, user-data-rights and user-profile in the order dsgvoSelfServiceFeatures used. billing-foundation requires tenant-lifecycle and compliance-profiles, which composeGdprStack({ tenantLifecycle: true }) mounts. user-profile in selfService requires user-data-rights-defaults and auth-email-password; composeUserDataRightsStack mounts the defaults, and the login comes from the auth option. Recipe: samples/recipes/compose-stacks.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: presets
  type: improvement
  title: securityBaselineFeatures and dsgvoSelfServiceFeatures are deprecated
  detail: Both presets stay for one release. Replace securityBaselineFeatures({ includeSessions }) with composeSecurityStack({ includeSessions }) and dsgvoSelfServiceFeatures({ userDataRights }) with composeGdprStack({ selfService: { userDataRights } }), both from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-dev-server/compose-stacks. The stacks mount the same features in the same order.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: runProdApp effectiveFeatures is deprecated
  detail: effectiveFeatures stays for one release. createTierEngineFeature({ tierMap }), or composeSaasStack, builds the per-tenant feature resolver at boot, and the prod-only features come from the mail, fileStorage and billing options.
  -->
- 2930518: Mail editor: informal German, tenant sender hint, readable button chips
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: document-designer
  type: fix
  title: Designer addresses the user informally in German, points tenant-routed senders to Email sending and renders chips inside buttons
  detail: All German document designer strings use du like the rest of the framework; the formal locale overrides keep Sie. For a notification with tenantTransport the sender hint in the mail editor says the address comes from the tenant's Email sending settings and links to that screen when the app mounts it; TemplateUsageEntry gains tenantTransport. A placeholder chip inside a button block is now drawn in inverted colors so the button text stays readable in the editor.
  -->
- 8ff5d19: Env blocks per feature and a typed composeEnvSchema
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: composeEnvSchema returns a typed schema
  detail: composeEnvSchema infers the merged shape from core, extend and every feature typed with featureWithEnvSchema(feature, schema), so parseEnv(composed.schema, …) returns typed values instead of a string record. optionalFeatures types those fields optional. A feature list widened to FeatureDefinition[] still compiles and contributes no keys to the type. extend may now repeat a feature's field when it is the same instance, so an app can spread a block such as stripeEnvSchema next to the mounted feature; a different field under that key still throws.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: crypto-shredding
  type: improvement
  title: kmsEnvSchema declares the subject-key KMS variables
  detail: kmsEnvSchema lists the 13 KMS slots (PLATFORM_KEK, its rotation predecessor and versions, KUMIKO_BLIND_INDEX_KEY, SUBJECT_KEYS_DATABASE_URL, the _CIPHERTEXT twins and the Key Manager coordinates), all optional. createCryptoShreddingFeature registers it, so composeEnvSchema picks it up.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: channel-email
  type: improvement
  title: smtpEnvSchema declares the SMTP_* variables
  detail: smtpEnvSchema covers SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_SECURE, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS and SMTP_FROM, all optional, and createChannelEmailFeature registers it. It lives next to createSmtpTransportFromEnv, which reads these variables.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: file-provider-s3
  type: improvement
  title: s3EnvSchema and createS3EnvSchema declare the S3 provider variables
  detail: s3EnvSchema covers S3_BUCKET, S3_REGION, S3_ACCESS_KEY, S3_SECRET_KEY, S3_ENDPOINT and S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE; createFileProviderS3Feature({ fromEnv: true }) registers it. createS3EnvSchema({ prefix }) builds the same block under another prefix, for example RELEASES_S3_. The endpoint must use https unless the host is loopback, and a blank endpoint counts as unset.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: subscription-stripe
  type: improvement
  title: stripeEnvSchema adds price slots to the Stripe env block
  detail: stripeEnvSchema({ prices: ["PRO", "TEAM"] }) returns the bridge keys plus one optional STRIPE_PRICE_<NAME> per price, each checked for the price_ prefix. Spread it into composeEnvSchema({ extend }) next to createSubscriptionStripeFeature; the shared bridge fields are no key clash.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: foundation-shared
  type: improvement
  title: buildInfoEnvSchema and demoAdminEnvSchema
  detail: buildInfoEnvSchema declares BUILD_VERSION and BUILD_TIME. demoAdminEnvSchema declares the seed logins DEMO_ADMIN_EMAIL and DEMO_SYSADMIN_EMAIL (required), their passwords (optional, at least 16 characters) and an optional DEMO_TENANT_ID. Apps add both through extend.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-mfa
  type: improvement
  title: MFA token secrets are optional and bound at boot
  detail: setupTokenSecret and challengeTokenSecret on createAuthMfaFeature are optional. Unset, the boot binds them through bindMfaTokenSecretsFromFeature(feature)(masterSecret, env): MFA_SETUP_TOKEN_SECRET and MFA_CHALLENGE_TOKEN_SECRET from env when set, otherwise derived from the master secret. mfaTokenSecretsEnvSchema declares both variables and the feature registers it next to the secrets master-key slot. A handler called before the binding throws instead of signing with an empty key.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: secrets
  type: improvement
  title: createSecretsFeature carries its env schema type
  detail: createSecretsFeature returns the feature typed with secretsEnvSchema, so composeEnvSchema types the KUMIKO_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY_* variables.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: improvement
  title: createAuthEmailPasswordFeature carries its env schema type
  detail: createAuthEmailPasswordFeature returns the feature typed with authEmailPasswordEnvSchema, so composeEnvSchema types JWT_SECRET and JWT_ISSUER.
  -->
- a02e354: legal-pages: terms routes, layout helper and boot seed
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: legal-pages
  type: improvement
  title: legal-pages serves terms of service, ships a layout helper and a boot seed
  detail: createLegalPagesFeature({ terms: true }) adds /legal/nutzungsbedingungen and /legal/terms (slug terms, de/en, never boot-required). createLegalPagesLayout({ siteName, css?, stylesheetHrefs?, headerHtml?, footerHtml?, contentClass? }) builds a wrapLayout with the app's chrome. legalContentSeed({ blocks } | { path }) returns a seed for runProdApp seeds that writes the blocks into SYSTEM_TENANT and updates existing ones, so the JSON stays authoritative. legalPagePath(routes, slug, lang) from the client-safe ./legal-pages/constants subpath gives static sites the same paths. Defaults are unchanged.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: server-runtime
  type: improvement
  title: runProdApp boot options for mail, kmsMode, fileStorage, billing, demoMode, seeds and signals
  detail: New optional runProdApp fields replace hand-wired bin/main.ts code. mail ({ transport: "smtp-env" | "inmemory" | EmailTransport, from?, resolveEmail?, tenantTransport? }) mounts channel-email and routes the auth mails through it; needs delivery. kmsMode ("required" | "optional" | { plaintextReason }) builds KMS and blind-index key from PLATFORM_KEK, SUBJECT_KEYS_DATABASE_URL and KUMIKO_BLIND_INDEX_KEY and cannot be combined with kms, blindIndexKey or allowPlaintextPii. fileStorage ({ provider: "s3-env" | "inmemory" | "auto" }) mounts the file provider; auto picks S3 when S3_* is complete and aborts a production boot on a partial S3 env; needs file-foundation. billing ({ stripe: { priceToTier, webhookPath? }, defaultTier }) mounts subscription-stripe and the tier-sync webhook route; needs billing-foundation and tier-engine. demoMode ({ readOnly, notice? }) serves GET /demo-mode and answers writes with 403 demo_read_only while readOnly; demo account credentials are published only when listed in notice.accounts. seeds also takes { demoTenant, demoAdminFromEnv, sysadminFromEnv, run }; the array form still works, but code indexing RunProdAppOptions["seeds"][number] must switch to ProdSeedFn. SIGTERM/SIGINT now run stop() with a 25 s drain timeout (signals: { drainTimeoutMs }) and exit 1 on timeout or error instead of always 0; signals: false hands the signals to the host. The env blocks the options read (SMTP_* for mail smtp-env, S3_* for fileStorage s3-env/auto, the KMS block for kmsMode, STRIPE_* for billing, DEMO_* for the seed shortcuts) join the app's envSchema for the boot dry run and the env validation without the app composing them; keys the option cannot run without (SMTP_HOST, the four S3 keys under s3-env, the seeded accounts) are required there. Without the new fields the boot behaves as before. createSubscriptionTierSync().createWebhookRoute takes an optional { path }. kmsEnvSchema is also exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/crypto-shredding/env, which loads without the crypto-shredding feature. The entity gains the status provisioned and the column provisionedAt, so apps that mount the feature generate a schema migration. kumiko ops waitlist-migrate --from offlot|publicstatus [--dry-run] copies a legacy waitlist table into the entity idempotently. Details in docs/guides/waitlist.md.
  migration: Apps that mount the waitlist feature run `kumiko schema generate <name>` and commit the migration: read_waitlist_entries gains the nullable column provisioned_at, and the status value provisioned is added. An app with its own waitlist (offlot-app, publicstatus, solon) mounts createWaitlistFeature() and copies the old rows with `kumiko ops waitlist-migrate --from offlot|publicstatus --dry-run` first. offlot-app keeps its legacy rows in the table read_waitlist_entries, the name the framework projection uses: copy or rename that table before the first boot and pass --source-table. The submit limit is keyed per IP and handler; behind a reverse proxy set trustedProxyHops, otherwise all visitors share one bucket of 5 submits per 10 minutes. With linkOnSignup the new consumer starts at the beginning of the event log and also provisions entries invited earlier.
  -->

## 0.369.0

### Minor Changes

- 57c0cff: Tenant admins edit their own mail server in the settings
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: mail-transport-smtp
  type: breaking
  title: Tenant admins edit their own SMTP server on the Email sending screen
  detail: mail-foundation's provider key and the SMTP keys (host, port, SSL/TLS, user name, sender address) carry settings masks, so the generated Settings-Hub shows tenant admins one Email sending form: the provider choice, the chosen provider's connection fields and its password, each field with a help text and every label in English, German and Spanish, saved together by one Save button in one /api/batch. Switching the provider swaps the fields at once; fields of a provider that is not selected are not saved. A selector owner's selection screen (`<owner>-tenant-selection`) now carries the plugins' config keys (field id `<owner>-<key>`) and secrets (field id `<plugin>-<key>`, listed in the new ConfigEditScreenDefinition.secretKeys) behind a visible condition on the provider field; the separate `<plugin>-tenant` and `<plugin>-tenant-secrets` screens and their dashboard panels are gone, and so is the `config.settings.saveProvider` label. A secret with its own writeRoles stays on the global secrets screen. Boot validation checks every secretKeys field (tenant scope, writeOnly text, declared secret). The configEdit renderer loads secretKeys fields from secrets:query:list (set or unset, no preview), writes them with secrets:write:set or secrets:write:delete in the same batch, and leaves hidden fields out. The provider key is no longer required: empty means the tenant has no own server and the platform sends, so readiness no longer reports it as missing (createTransportForTenant still throws on an empty provider). The provider and SMTP keys are written by TenantAdmin and the system identity, no longer by SystemAdmin, because a platform-level provider would reach every tenant without that tenant's password. The secrets set and delete handlers also admit the system identity, so server code stores a tenant secret via dispatchSystemWrite through the same key and value checks as an admin; the settings screens keep showing only the human roles. The provider choice shows each plugin's `<feature>.settings` name, also for a plugin without settings of its own, and keeps the English name when a locale feature mounted earlier declares the same key in its own language only. A MailTransportPlugin with `selectableInSettings: false` stays allowed on the server but is not offered in the form; the in-memory transport sets it, because apps mount it next to smtp in production and a tenant admin picking it would drop every mail. A plugin's secrets section takes an optional `<feature>.settings.secrets` title (SMTP password under "SMTP sign-in").
  migration: E2E specs that used the testIds `dashboard-panel-<plugin>-tenant`, `dashboard-panel-<plugin>-tenant-secrets` or the separate secret input of these screens address the fields of `<owner>-tenant-selection` instead (one Save). Code that wrote these keys as a SystemAdmin user writes them as the tenant's TenantAdmin or via dispatchSystemWrite. Apps that relied on readiness flagging an empty provider check it themselves.
  -->

With tenantTransport set, transport may be omitted: a mail that then has no transport fails with missing_credentials instead of throwing. The template test mail (template-resolver send-test) now gets the tenant config in its channel context and uses the template's notification, so it leaves through the same transport as the real mail.

  detail: Both handlers ran on the boot database connection, so in an /api/batch a later failing command rolled back the config writes but kept the stored secret. ## 0.368.0

### Minor Changes

- 39b5de4: cap-counter: a reservation can be consumed per unit through a public handle, so jobs that learn their quantity at runtime stay under the hard cap
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-counter
  type: improvement
  title: calendarCapReservationHandle consumes a reservation per unit
  detail: |
    `reserveCalendarCapUsage` now returns `reservationId`. `calendarCapReservationHandle(ctx, reservationId, { capName, periodStartIso })` returns a handle with `consume(units)` (turns reserved units into booked ones, counter unchanged) and `release()` (gives back the unconsumed rest). A handler reserves the worst case before the job is dispatched, the job consumes per written unit, so parallel dispatches can no longer overshoot the hard cap and a retry only counts what was written.
  
    `consume` beyond the still-reserved rest throws `CapReservationOverConsumedError` (422, `cap_reservation_over_consumed`). `consume` against a settle tombstone throws `CapReservationSettledError` (422, `cap_reservation_settled`); `release` against it is a no-op. When the reservation outlived its TTL and was swept, `consume` books the units directly, the way settle does for a missing row, without a hard-cap check.
  -->
- 1a1b772: cap-counter: a TTL sweep or release of a partly consumed calendar reservation no longer makes a later settle or consume count the consumed units twice
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-counter
  type: fix
  title: Swept or released calendar reservations remember the units consume booked
  detail: |
    The reservation row now stores `consumed_amount`. A release or the TTL sweep gives back only the unconsumed rest. If units were consumed, it keeps the row as a released tombstone (`released_at` set, `amount` 0) until the tombstone TTL passes, instead of deleting it. A later `settle` subtracts the consumed units from the booking, and a `consume` after the sweep books its units directly and is remembered the same way, so the counter ends at exactly the settled total. `settle` below the consumed units throws `CapSettleBelowConsumedError` (422, `cap_settle_below_consumed`) in every state. Expired released tombstones are deleted by the sweep.
  migration: Apps with cap-counter generate a migration for the new columns store_cap_reservations.consumed_amount (integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0) and store_cap_reservations.released_at (kumiko migrate generate).
  -->
- 7949df2: Bundled features are mounted through create*Feature() factories, the two S3 providers merge into createFileProviderS3Feature({ fromEnv }), and @app/define with kumiko codegen is removed
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Bundled feature constants become create*Feature() factories
  detail: |
    Every bundled feature that was mounted as a constant (tagsFeature, ledgerFeature, authFoundationFeature, ...) now has a create<Name>Feature() factory exported from the same subpath, and apps mount `createTagsFeature()` instead of `tagsFeature`. Factories of features without options take no arguments; the ones that already had options keep them. Two calls of a factory give interchangeable instances, so mounting the same feature from two stacks does not trip the "mounted twice as distinct instances" check.
  
    The old constants keep working as deprecated aliases and are removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.
  
    old -> new:
      tagsFeature -> createTagsFeature()
      ledgerFeature -> createLedgerFeature()
      authFoundationFeature -> createAuthFoundationFeature()
      fooBarFeature -> createFooBarFeature() (same rule for every bundled feature constant)
      typeof tagsFeature -> ReturnType<typeof createTagsFeature>
  migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It renames the imports and replaces every use with the factory call. It reports aliased imports, re-exports, namespace access, dynamic imports and files that compare a feature by identity with file and line; handle those by hand (one factory call per mount, or keep one shared instance).
  codemod: scripts/codemod/feature-factory.ts
  -->

  feature: file-provider-s3
  type: breaking
  title: The S3 file providers merge into createFileProviderS3Feature({ fromEnv })
  detail: |
    createFileProviderS3Feature() mounts the per-tenant config provider as before. createFileProviderS3Feature({ fromEnv: true }) mounts the env-configured provider (feature name, provider key "s3-env" and requires unchanged). The S3 client helpers (createS3Provider, createS3ProviderFromEnv, parseS3EnvConfig, resolveForcePathStyle, S3ProviderConfig) move to the new subpath @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/file-provider-s3/lib.
  
    The subpaths file-provider-s3-env and files-provider-s3 keep working as deprecated re-exports and are removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.
  
    old -> new:
      fileProviderS3EnvFeature from .../file-provider-s3-env -> createFileProviderS3Feature({ fromEnv: true }) from .../file-provider-s3
      fileProviderS3Feature -> createFileProviderS3Feature()
      @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/files-provider-s3 -> @cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/file-provider-s3/lib
  migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It rewrites the imports and the env feature mount, and reports `typeof fileProviderS3EnvFeature` and re-exports of it with file and line.
  codemod: scripts/codemod/s3-imports.ts
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: dev-server
  type: breaking
  title: @app/define and kumiko codegen are removed
  detail: |
    The .kumiko/ codegen (define.ts, types.generated.d.ts, schemas.generated.ts) is gone: runCodegen, scanEvents and their types are no longer exported, the dev server no longer watches r.defineEvent calls, `kumiko codegen` is removed, `kumiko-build --check` is removed and kumiko-build no longer runs a codegen pass. The scaffolded .gitignore no longer lists .kumiko/, so the upgrade marker .kumiko/upgrade-state.json can be committed. ctx.appendEvent stays bound to the augmentable KumikoEventTypeMap; to emit an event with a payload checked against its definition use emitEvent(ctx, eventDef, { aggregateId, aggregateType, payload, headers? }) with the EventDef that r.defineEvent returns (emitEvent now also accepts headers).
  migration: Replace `@app/define` imports with direct framework imports (defineWriteHandler/defineQueryHandler/defineFeature from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine, events via r.defineEvent and emitEvent) and drop the `file:./.kumiko` dependency plus the bunfig/tsconfig resolver entries.   detail: |
    A personal field with a nullable owner can now declare `personal: { of: "ownerId", whenAbsent: "self" }` (entity fields and `defineEvent` piiFields). While the owner is empty, the value is encrypted under `record:<entity>:<id>`, the same subject as `personal: "self"` on events and `personal: { of: "id" }` on entities. `forget-subject` on that record then erases the value, its blind index and its search document; with `"tenant"` the value stayed readable until the tenant was destroyed. A row can mix subjects: the ciphertext names its key inline, so owner-keyed, tenant-keyed and record-keyed fields decrypt side by side.
  
    The boot validator accepts "self" next to "tenant" and rejects it on `idType: "serial"` entities, because a forget-subject request needs a UUID record id. Owner transitions behave as for "tenant": when an update assigns an owner (absent to X) the value moves from the record key to the user key; the created event stays record-keyed. The data-retention hardDelete also erases the record key of an ownerless "self" row; a row with an owner keeps its owner key.
  migration: |
    Switching an existing field from `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to `"self"` changes only new writes. Events and rows written earlier stay tenant-keyed (still readable) until the PII event backfill re-keys them. The backfill fingerprint is bumped (`owner-rekey-v2`), so the boot-time backfill runs one more full pass: tenant-keyed values of rows without an owner move under their record key, tenant-keyed values of rows with an owner still move under that owner. The pass rewrites event payloads in place through the existing backfill path and queues the affected projections for rebuild. Apps that run the backfill manually call `backfillEventPiiEncryption` with `resolveOwnerFromProjection: true, rekeyTenantKeyedOwnerFields: true`, then rebuild the projections. Values of a record forgotten earlier become `[[erased]]`. The re-key covers entity lifecycle events only: custom `defineEvent` piiFields that switch from `whenAbsent: "tenant"` to `"self"` keep their old events tenant-keyed.
  
    Old events are never reinterpreted at read time: an old created event of a row that got an owner later keeps its record key until a forget of that record, which erases it, while the later owner-keyed copies stay readable.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- fbc0759: One DB connection factory: createDbConnection({ url, ... }) on postgres-js, and the query helpers move from the bun-db subpath into the db subpath
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: createDbConnection({ url, ... }) is the only connection factory, query helpers move from /bun-db to /db
  detail: |
    postgres-js is the only DB driver. createDbConnection takes one options object, is synchronous and accepts the new options ssl and onNotice. The Bun.SQL provider, createConnection, createPgConnection and DB_PROVIDER are removed. The query helpers (selectMany, insertOne, transaction, asRawClient, ...) keep their API and are now exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db. The `tx` handed to the transaction() callback is typed as DbTx (the postgres-js transaction handle it always was at runtime) instead of the Bun.SQL instance type; a helper that takes `db: DbConnection` and receives that tx needs `DbRunner` or `DbTx`.
  
    The positional form createDbConnection(url, options) and the @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/bun-db subpath keep working as deprecated aliases and are removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.
  
    old -> new:
      createConnection(url, options) (async) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options }) (sync)
      createPgConnection(url, options) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options })
      createDbConnection(url, options) -> createDbConnection({ url, ...options }) (positional form is deprecated)
      @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/bun-db -> @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/db (deprecated alias until the first release after 2026-10-29)
  
    Removed without replacement: createBunDbConnection, bunDbConnectionOptionsFromEnv, the BunDbConnection, BunDbTx, BunDbRunner and BunDbConnectionOptions types, DbPoolHandle (use DbConnectionHandle), the PgListenClient re-export from /bun-db (import it from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/db-connection) and the DB_PROVIDER environment variable.
  migration: Run `bun kumiko-upgrade --apply`. It rewrites bun-db imports to /db, createDbConnection(url, options) and createConnection/createPgConnection calls to the object form, and reports leftovers (removed Bun.SQL exports, DB_PROVIDER) with file and line. Remove DB_PROVIDER from your env files.
  codemod: scripts/codemod/db-factory.ts
  -->

The erasure now appends the status-deleted user.updated event to that stream too, so the login door closes, the handler returns 200 and a read_users rebuild keeps the state.

Provider contexts (FileProviderContext, MailTransportContext, InboundMailContext) keep their own _userId. JobContext._userId is unchanged.

## 0.367.0

### Minor Changes

- f6b1803: Email channel can send through the tenant's own mail provider
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: channel-email
  type: improvement
  title: Email channel can send through the tenant's own mail provider
  detail: EmailChannelOptions gets tenantTransport, a resolver called per send with the delivery channel context. mail-foundation exports tenantMailTransport for it: a tenant with a provider configured sends through its own transport, a broken provider fails the send, a tenant without a provider uses the app transport. The transport is built per send and never cached, and the tenant comes from the server-side delivery context only. ChannelContext now carries the tenant's config accessor as config. Without tenantTransport nothing changes.
  -->
- f6b1803: Notifications can keep their mail template system-only
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: improvement
  title: Notifications can keep their mail template system-only
  detail: r.notification(name, { systemOnly: true }) marks the stored mail template as a platform text. Tenant admins no longer see it in the template overview, list or detail, and creating a tenant version (upsert-tenant, copy-locale, import-bundle, also a SystemAdmin writing for a tenant) is refused with access_denied and templateResolver.errors.systemOnlyTemplate. SystemAdmins edit the system template as before, and the mail renderer always uses it, even if a tenant row exists from before.
  -->
- f6b1803: Delivery signs unsubscribe links itself
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: Delivery signs unsubscribe links itself
  detail: r.notification(name, { unsubscribe: true }) makes delivery put a signed data.unsubscribeUrl into every email of that notification when the service has unsubscribeLinks. User recipients get a user token, route recipients an address token (only with a blind-index key, otherwise no link). The token is scoped to tenant, notification and channel; a link the caller passes in data.unsubscribeUrl wins. runProdApp option unsubscribe: { secret } mounts createUnsubscribeRoutes and wires the links; the base URL comes from auth.publicOrigin, auth.mail.baseUrl or APP_BASE_URL, and without one boot warns and no link is added.
  -->
- f6b1803: Template bundles with a logo can be seeded
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: improvement
  title: Template bundles with a logo can be seeded
  detail: seedSystemTemplateBundle(db, bundle, { dispatcher }) now seeds bundles that carry resources such as a logo by running the import-bundle-system write on the given seed dispatcher. With ifExists "skip" (default) nothing is written when every locale row already exists; if only some exist, the whole bundle is imported again. Without a dispatcher such a bundle still fails with a message that names the missing option.
  -->
- f6b1803: Template conditions with data-if and a percent variable type
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: improvement
  title: Template conditions with data-if and a percent variable type
  detail: A paragraph, heading or table row with data-if="name" renders only when the variable has a value (0 counts as a value); inside a repeat row the name refers to the row field, on the repeat row itself to the root variable. The sanitizer keeps the attribute, and template validation reports a condition on an undeclared variable. New variable type percent (templateVariable.percent()) takes percentage points and renders locale-aware, 12 as "12 %" in German and "12%" in English; the preview uses its example value. The document designer has no toolbar control for conditions yet; the attribute survives editing.
  -->
- 5f2cc2f: Unsubscribe links use the tenant's host and the mail's language, apps learn about address opt-outs
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: Unsubscribe links use the tenant's host and the mail's language, apps learn about address opt-outs
  detail: unsubscribeLinks and the runProdApp option unsubscribe take tenantOrigin, an app callback that returns the sending tenant's own origin (subdomain or custom domain) per send; null, a throw or a non-https value fall back to the app origin and never fail the send. The signed token now carries the mail's locale (notify option locale), so the confirmation, result and undo pages render in that language; tokens without it keep working and show English. A form post to the resubscribe route now answers with an HTML page, JSON callers are unchanged. After a committed address opt-out an app job declared with trigger on DeliveryHandlers.unsubscribeAddress receives addressHash, notificationType and channel (unsubscribeAddressPayloadSchema) with the tenant in ctx.triggeredBy.tenantId; hashUnsubscribeAddress(email) matches it to the app's own subscriber. UNSUBSCRIBE_PAGE_EN exports the English page texts, German and Spanish come with the locale packages.
  -->

  detail: |
    r.writeHandler, r.queryHandler, r.entity, r.requires and r.hook now take one object. The positional overloads are gone from the types and throw when the feature is defined, with a message that points at the codemod. The throw is removed in the first release after 2026-10-29.

HookDefinition and EntityObjectDefinition are exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types. Hook definitions are checked per type: validation takes no escapeHatch, phase only exists on postSave and postDelete, and { allOf } is not accepted on preSave.

Calls it cannot resolve statically (a spread argument, a registrar that is not typed as FeatureRegistrar) are listed as manual work with file and line; rewrite those by hand.

  -->

## 0.365.1

### Patch Changes

- 9a8abc9: eraseKey tombstones never-keyed subjects
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: crypto-shredding
  type: fix
  title: eraseKey leaves a tombstone for subjects that never had a key
  detail: eraseKey now records an erased entry even when the subject has no key (pre-KMS plaintext). A later createKey or write for that subject fails with subject_erased instead of minting a fresh key and re-encrypting the plaintext. Erase flows must write with writePurpose erasure after eraseKey. kumiko_subject_keys now gets one tombstone row per forgotten record subject and per step dispatch. The tenant destruction stage tenant-row now fails loudly when marking the tenant destroyed does not succeed.
  migration: Run backfill-pii before erasing Pre-KMS data, otherwise untouched plaintext stays readable after eraseKey.
  -->
- 8633239: step-dispatcher delivers through a BullMQ job
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: step-dispatcher
  type: fix
  title: step-dispatcher delivers each dispatch as a retried job, so a slow receiver no longer delays other tenants
  detail: The step-dispatcher projection now only enqueues one `step-dispatcher:job:deliver` job per dispatch request, and the job performs the webhook or mail delivery. Redis holds only the dispatch stream id and the tenant, never the request payload. Transient failures (network error, timeout, 5xx, 408, 429, any mail adapter failure) are retried 3 times with exponential backoff; the outcome event and the payload key erase follow after the final attempt. Permanent failures (invalid url, blocked host, other 4xx, unavailable auth secret) are recorded at once. At most 2 deliveries per tenant run at the same time, so one tenant's slow receivers cannot hold up the others. This corrects the 0.346.0 note that a hanging receiver no longer stalls the dispatcher for every tenant: the shared consumer still delivered one request at a time.
  migration: step-dispatcher now needs a job runner (Redis) and a worker consuming the default worker lane. Without a job runner the projection throws instead of delivering. Test stacks must pass `jobs` to setupTestStack and call `drainJobs()` after the event dispatcher ran. `r.job` accepts `maxPerTenant: { limit, onLimit: "defer", deferMs? }`; a plain number still drops excess enqueues. A `webhook.send` request that gets a retryable status (5xx, 408, 429) is now sent up to 4 times under the same Idempotency-Key. Worker pods must know the deliver job before the projection enqueues it, so deploy worker and API together or the worker first. A dev server only consumes jobs when the app mounts `createJobsFeature()`.
  -->

- 72a5c9c: Migration notes for boot checks that were released as fixes
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Boot checks from the review round 1 release reject configurations that used to boot
  detail: |
    These checks shipped as fixes without migration notes. Each one throws for a configuration that was accepted before:
    - a where-rule subquery on a table whose columns cannot be derived
    - a drawer prefill that targets a sensitive field or a field the form does not render
    - two secret fields with the same id
    - access.personalData "public-intake" combined with rateLimit: { disabled: true }
    - a recordOwned field on an entity with idType "serial"
    - dedupeFeatures for same-named features with different registrations
    The agent-tools manifest check in buildToolCatalog throws when the catalog is built for a request, not at boot.
  migration: |
    Boot every app against the new version before rolling it out, and send one agent tool request if the app mounts agent-tools. Give where-rule subqueries a table with derivable columns, prefill only rendered non-sensitive fields, make secret field ids unique, give public-intake handlers a rateLimit that is not disabled, switch recordOwned entities to idType "uuid" or change the field's personal stance, and rename or align duplicated features.
  -->
- 7aa3223: Bun.SQL provider parity
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Bun.SQL provider parity fixes for DB_PROVIDER=bun
  detail: Array params bind as Postgres array literals, transaction handles are detected correctly, Instant params are stored at millisecond precision, integer params reject fractions, and migrations hold their advisory lock on one pinned connection. LISTEN/NOTIFY uses Bun.SQL listen() on its own connection, which the pool idle timeout does not close, so the Bun provider no longer opens a postgres-js peer.
  -->
- eef5ff1: Handlers wrapped with withCapEnforcement or withRollingCapEnforcement can no longer run as nested writes
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-counter
  type: breaking
  title: Handlers wrapped with withCapEnforcement or withRollingCapEnforcement are rejected when called through a nested ctx.write
  detail: Since the wrappers reserve through reserveBeforeTransaction, the dispatcher rejects a nested ctx.write, ctx.writeAs or handler-to-handler call of such a handler with an internal error ("has a pre-transaction phase ... cannot run as a nested write") instead of running it. Before the reservation lifecycle change the wrapped handler ran normally when called nested.
  migration: Dispatch rolling- and calendar-capped handlers only as top-level commands (HTTP write or batch). A handler that calls one through ctx.write declares the cap on itself instead, or the call moves out of the handler into a client or job that dispatches a top-level command.
  -->

  detail: When a tenant copies a locale from the system default, the image and attachment files are now read and written to the tenant's storage in a beforeTransaction phase. - fbc6938: Erasure writes store the erased sentinel instead of failing on a deleted subject key
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Executor update and delete with writePurpose erasure, and forget, write the erased sentinel for subjects whose key is gone
  detail: Re-encrypting a pre-KMS plaintext row after eraseKey threw subject-erased, so the erase flows could not finish their own follow-up writes. Update and delete with writePurpose erasure, and forget always, now replace the PII fields of an erased subject in changes and previous with the sentinel; fields of other subjects in the same row stay encrypted. Without writePurpose and for restore the subject-erased conflict stays. The forget-subject door close and the forget cleanup pass writePurpose erasure to the user lifecycle update.
  -->
- eef5ff1: Feature-toggle snapshot loads are serialized and createFeatureToggleRuntime can share the server's cache-sync bus

  type: fix
  title: Overlapping toggle refreshes no longer drop a flip, and the runtime can reuse the server cache-sync bus
  detail: initialize() and refresh() now run one snapshot load at a time, so a flip applied while a second load is in flight is kept instead of being overwritten by older rows. createFeatureToggleRuntime takes an optional fourth cacheSyncBus argument; with it no second bus (and no extra Redis connections) is created and close() leaves the shared bus open.
  migration: Pass the server's cache-sync bus as the fourth argument of createFeatureToggleRuntime to avoid the additional Redis publisher and subscriber connections of the default bus; without it the runtime still builds and closes its own bus.
  -->
- 80e2132: Erasure jobs delete the bytes of files that a tenant handover moved into the tenant
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Soft-delete cleanup and hardDelete retention delete the bytes of handed-over files
  detail: A tenant handover moves a fileRef row to the new tenant, but its storageKey keeps the previous tenant's prefix. The soft-delete cleanup and the data-retention hardDelete went through `ctx.files.ref()` and `ctx.files.list()`, which reject keys outside the job's tenant, so the bytes and derivatives of such files were never deleted and the soft-delete cleanup kept the row forever. Both now delete through the new `deleteFileRefBytes(files, row, context)` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/derivatives`, built on the new `FileContext.listFromFileRef(row)` (the row's key plus its derivatives, under the same trust as `refFromFileRef`). Form-draft discard deletes draft files through `refFromFileRef` as well.
  -->

  detail: createAuthRoutes throws when mfaVerifyHandler is set without switchTenantMfaGateHandler, and runDevApp and runProdApp check that the gate handler is registered before wiring, so a missing gate can no longer let switch-tenant skip MFA. Setups that set mfaVerifyHandler must also register the switch-tenant gate handler.

- cd16f29: resource-upload, import-bundle and import-bundle-system move their storage I/O in front of the transaction
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: breaking
  title: resource-upload, import-bundle and import-bundle-system upload in a beforeTransaction phase and can no longer run as nested writes
  detail: The three handlers now validate and upload their files before the write transaction opens and only create the fileRef and template rows inside it, so no database connection sits idle in a transaction during storage I/O. A rolled-back transaction releases the uploaded bytes. Because they now have a pre-transaction phase, the dispatcher rejects a nested ctx.write, ctx.writeAs or handler-to-handler call of them ("has a pre-transaction phase"). The exported storeTemplateResource is replaced by prepareTemplateResourceBeforeTransaction (beforeTransaction half) and storePreparedTemplateResource (in-transaction half).
  migration: Dispatch resource-upload, import-bundle and import-bundle-system as top-level commands, or from a perCommand handler via ctx.write. A handler that called them nested moves that call into a client or job, or becomes a perCommand handler. Code that called storeTemplateResource calls prepareTemplateResourceBeforeTransaction in a beforeTransaction phase and passes the result to storePreparedTemplateResource in the handler.
  -->
- 2a33c8d: Tenant destruction sweep splits one tick budget across all destroying tenants
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant-lifecycle
  type: fix
  title: One sweep tick shares a single stage budget between all destroying tenants
  detail: The destruction sweep used to give every destroying tenant its own full stage budget, so a few large tenants stretched one tick far beyond the minute cron window and the following ticks were skipped. The tick budget is now divided evenly over the destroying tenants. Each tenant's slice starts when that tenant's turn begins, so an overrun by one tenant never leaves the next ones with a zero slice. runNextDestructionStage accepts an optional deadlineAt.
  -->

  detail: afterCommit seed hooks now get a notify function bound to the signup dispatcher's job runner when the dispatcher provides one, falling back to the regular factory. The afterCommit hook context is built only when the hook actually runs.
  -->

Inviting an email that already is a member of the target tenant fails with 422 waitlist_not_invitable, as reject already did.

  detail: createWaitlistFeature({ emailRateLimits: [] }) no longer fails boot validation; the per-email bucket is dropped as documented. notifyRecipient runs before the per-email advisory lock and the entry insert, so a failing resolver can no longer abort the submit transaction or hold the lock; a throwing resolver only skips the admin notice. The duplicate check queries status pending or invited with limit 1 instead of scanning the first 50 rows of the address. The feature description now states that the response body is identical for known and unknown addresses while response timing can differ.
