## 0.364.0

### Minor Changes

- 6b1567e: CapExceededError carries resetAt and retryAfterSeconds, API sets Retry-After
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-counter
  type: breaking
  title: CapExceededError carries resetAt and retryAfterSeconds, API sets Retry-After
  migration: |
    Periodic caps no longer need RateLimitError({ windowSeconds: 0, ... }). Where you catch CapExceededError from enforceCap and rethrow it as RateLimitError, drop the catch and let CapExceededError pass: the response stays 429 with a correct Retry-After, error.code becomes cap_exceeded instead of rate_limited, and error.details carries resetAt and retryAfterSeconds. Keep a feature-specific message with enforceCap({ ..., i18nKey }) and pass a period end other than the calendar month with periodEndIso (e.g. a budget's resetsAtIso). Clients matching on rate_limited for these caps must also accept cap_exceeded. Any KumikoError with retryAfterSeconds (including RateLimitError thrown in a handler) now gets a Retry-After header from /api/write, /api/batch and /api/query.
  -->
- c181b3f: Document designer editors follow the approved board
  
  Mail-layout templates accept appearance meta (width, font, outer background, accent line, button style) that the mail renderer applies, and the layout-source query returns it. The layout editor uses the shared editor shell with one paper and one shared toolbar (`DocumentContentEditor` gains `toolbarHost`). Mail and PDF editors share frame, info bar, rails and footer.
  
  The unused `sender` key of mail template meta is gone from the editor; stored rows that still carry it are read without it, so they stay editable.
  
  Invalid template meta now reports per-field messages (`templateResolver.errors.template.meta.<field>.required|invalid`) instead of the parser text; the editors show them at the field. The `tenant-overrides` query additionally returns one row per customising tenant (name, status, version, changed at/by) and, with `diffTenantId`, the diff to the system version. A language without a version shows an empty state in the mail editor instead of a disabled editor.
  
  The `compileDocumentBody` option `resourceImageMaxWidthPx` caps resource images in mails (180 px). The `send-test` command takes `prefixSubject` (default true) to skip the `[TEST]` subject prefix, the template preview returns `mailLayout` (slug, scope, version of the layout used), and `RenderedMail` carries the layout ref.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: document-designer
  type: improvement
  title: Document designer editors follow the approved board
  -->
- 8e81d73: Removed the DocumentRepeatRow alias
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: breaking
  title: DocumentRepeatRow is removed, use DocumentTableRow
  migration: |
    Replace `DocumentRepeatRow` with `DocumentTableRow` (identical shape).
  -->
- 8e81d73: SecretsContext.withRunner binds secret reads and writes to a transaction
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: secrets
  type: improvement
  title: SecretsContext.withRunner(tx) runs secret access on a given transaction
  detail: The OAuth refresh now reads and writes the refresh token on its advisory-lock transaction, so a refresh holds one pool connection instead of two and parallel refreshes cannot starve the pool. Custom SecretsContext implementations need a `withRunner` method.
  -->
- 68078ee: A draft no longer replaces the active template
  
  Saving a draft over an active template now stores it beside the active version (new column draft) instead of overwriting it; publish promotes the draft, the new handlers discard-draft and discard-draft-system throw it away. find-by-id and layout-source return the working version (open draft, else the stored one) with active { version, since }; overview rows gain draftVersion and activeSince. The resolver keeps serving the active version.
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: breaking
  title: A draft no longer replaces the active template
  detail: Saving a draft (upsert-tenant default, copy-locale, import-bundle with status draft) over an active template stores it beside the active version in the new column draft instead of overwriting content, meta and status; resolveTemplate, resolveLayout, preview without content and sends keep using the active version. publish and publish-system promote an open draft (the publish gate checks the draft) and record activeVersion and activeSince; the new handlers discard-draft and discard-draft-system drop it and refuse with no_draft when none is open. find-by-id and layout-source return the working version (the open draft with status draft, else the stored one) plus active { version, since }, null when nothing is served. overview keeps status and version of the served version and adds draftVersion and activeSince. A draft over a row that is not active (new, draft or archived) behaves as before. A tenant never sees system draft content: find-by-id, layout-source, overview, copy-locale and diff-to-system apply a system draft only for a SystemAdmin and hide system rows that were never served; list leaves those rows out too. Version numbers shown for an active row are the served version (activeVersion): resolveTemplate / resolveLayout results, tenant-overrides rows and the override diff no longer show the save counter that drafts raise.
  migration: |
    Run kumiko schema generate and apply the migration before deploying: it adds the nullable columns draft, active_version and active_since to read_template_resources. No rebuild needed.
  -->
- b5a6395: templateVariable.richText declares a notification variable that carries sanitized HTML
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: improvement
  title: templateVariable.richText for notification variables that carry formatted HTML
  detail: Notification variables are escaped, so a value holding HTML (for example a document written in a rich text editor) showed up as literal tags in the mail. A variable declared with templateVariable.richText({ required }) is run through the document sanitizer at render time and inserted as HTML; bold, italic, lists and safe links stay, script, event handlers and javascript links are not emitted as markup. If the sanitizer rejects a value, it is rendered as escaped text and a warning with the violation codes is logged. All other variable types stay escaped.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 15039ce: Audit list pagination
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: audit
  type: fix
  title: Audit list pages by id unless sorted by type
  detail: An explicit createdAt sort pages in id order so keyset pagination no longer skips rows.
  -->
- 8e81d73: Auth gate falls back to the built-in login when the loginUrl builder fails
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: fix
  title: A loginUrl builder that throws no longer crashes the app tree
  detail: The auth gate resolves the login redirect once per location change and, when the builder returns an invalid URL or throws, logs the error and shows the built-in login screen instead of throwing during render.
  -->
- a0dcd31: Migration recipe for apps that rendered auth mails with the render*Email helpers removed in 0.363.0
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: fix
  title: How to send an auth mail after the render*Email helpers were removed in 0.363.0
  detail: No runtime change. The 0.363.0 breaking entry lists renderActivationEmail, renderResetPasswordEmail, renderUnlockAccountEmail, renderVerifyEmail and renderInviteEmail as removed but does not say how app code that rendered one of these mails itself now sends it. This entry adds that recipe.
  migration: |
    App code that rendered an auth mail itself and passed the result as `data`, for example `notify("auth-email-password:signup-activation", { route: { email }, data: renderActivationEmail({ url, expiresAt, locale, appName }), priority: "critical" })`, breaks twice since 0.363.0: the helper is gone and the notification type is now `auth-email-password:notify:signup-activation`. The stored template renders subject and body; the app only passes template variables.
    For a signup activation link, call `issueSignupActivation({ redis, notify: ctx.notify, email, appUrl, appName, locale, timeZone, tokenTtlMinutes, onTokenStored })` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/auth-email-password` (only redis, notify, email and appUrl are required). It drops any live signup token for the email, stores a new one under the keys signup-confirm reads and sends the mail. `appUrl` is the bare activation page; a function `(locale) => url` picks the page per locale.
    If the app stores the token itself and only needs the mail, call `ctx.notify(AuthMailNotificationTypes.signupActivation, { route: { email }, data: { appName, actionUrl, validFor, validUntil }, locale, priority: "critical" })`. `AuthMailNotificationTypes` comes from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/auth-email-password`. All four variables are required strings: ctx.notify checks them against the declared template variables and throws an InternalError on a missing or invalid one, which fails the write. `actionUrl` is the page URL with `token=<encodeURIComponent(token)>` appended as a query parameter and must be an http, https or mailto URL. `validFor` and `validUntil` come from `tokenMailExpiry({ expiresAt, issuedAt, timeZone }, locale)` in `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/auth-email-password/email-templates`. Only send a `locale` that has a template for the type, because the renderer has no locale fallback and a locale without a template sends nothing: use `resolveMailLocale(locale)` when `hasMailTranslationKey(resolveMailLocale(locale), "auth.mail.activation.subject")` is true (both from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/i18n`), otherwise `"en"`. The other mails use the subject keys `auth.mail.reset.subject`, `auth.mail.unlock.subject`, `auth.mail.verify.subject` and `auth.mail.invite.subject`.
    The other auth mails work the same way with `AuthMailNotificationTypes.passwordReset`, `.accountUnlock`, `.emailVerification` and `.invite`; the invite mail also needs a `role` variable.
  -->

  title: seedAdminGuarded rewrites the admin email only when its blind index is missing or stale
  detail: rewriteSeededUserEmail returns early when the stored email blind index already matches the expected value, so repeated boots no longer re-encrypt the email and grow the user event stream. The row version is now checked with a type guard instead of a cast.

  detail: A SystemAdmin writing a config value for another tenant previously handed the validator a system-mode db that could read every tenant. `ConfigValidateContext.db` is now a `TenantDb` locked to the tenant the value is written for. The validator runs inside the write transaction, so a slow query there should set its own timeout.

Each row of `termsParagraphs` is now a richText value: bold, italic and http(s)/mailto/tel links render as HTML, headings become bold rows. Author HTML and images in the terms stay escaped text, and links outside those schemes stay "label (url)". Tenant overrides of the template keep working, the variable name and row structure are unchanged.

The canvas reserves the footer margin like the renderer. - b13c0d4: Regression tests: Art. 17 forget shreds PII in user.updated previous payloads
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: user-data-rights
  type: fix
  title: Regression tests prove that forget also shreds the previous email in user.updated events
  detail: No runtime change. Integration tests with a configured subject KMS show that after an email change followed by forget, the old and new email in user.updated changes and previous decrypt only to the erased sentinel and the subject key is gone. Without a configured KMS, event payloads stay plaintext by design.

- fd5009a: forget-subject closes the user's login before the derived-data sweep and commits it independently
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: crypto-shredding
  type: fix
  title: forget-subject keeps the user status flip and PAT revocation when the sweep fails
  detail: The user is set to Deleted and its personal access tokens are revoked right after the key erase, in their own transaction on the outside-transaction db. A failing blind-index or search sweep still makes the handler throw so the cleanup can be retried, but it no longer rolls the login door back. Without an outside-transaction db the previous in-transaction savepoint path is used. A failure while closing the login door of an existing user now fails the forget (retry is safe) instead of passing silently; subjects without a user row are skipped.
  -->
- 8fb6aa6: Handler field references support business keys and array fields

- 7482ee2: Termination receipt limit no longer keys Redis by an unkeyed email hash
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: billing-foundation
  type: fix
  title: The termination receipt rate limit keys Redis with a keyed, handler-bound digest instead of an unkeyed SHA-256 of the email
  detail: HandlerContext gains an optional rateLimitDigest(value), an HMAC bound to the running handler, so a handler can build rate-limit keys without plaintext identifiers and cannot reproduce the dispatcher's payload-bucket digests. normalizePayloadBucketValue is exported from the pipeline entry point. The receipt limit reuses it, and withholds the receipt mail (the declaration is still recorded) when no digest is wired. Payload-bucket normalization now applies Unicode NFKC first, so fullwidth lookalikes share a bucket. Existing receipt buckets restart empty; they expire after the 24 hour window.
  -->

  type: fix
  title: Stale-run sweep uses the job-run retention window for queued runs
  detail: The sweep now only fails queued runs that are older than the configured retention days instead of every queued run past the stale cutoff, so freshly queued runs of a long backlog are no longer failed.
  -->
- 8be3807: Stripe customer portal reports an unknown customer as a business error
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: subscription-stripe
  type: fix
  title: A stale Stripe customer id no longer turns the customer portal into a 500
  detail: createPortalSession now maps Stripe's "No such customer" rejection (account switch, customer deleted in the dashboard) to an UnprocessableError with the i18n key billing-foundation.errors.providerCustomerUnknown, translated in German and Spanish, instead of letting the raw Stripe error surface as a server error.
  -->
- 8e81d73: copy-locale and export-bundle handle system sources and mixed formats
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: fix
  title: copy-locale ignores archived tenant sources and duplicates linked files of system sources; export-bundle refuses locales with differing format
  detail: copy-locale no longer copies from an archived tenant template, and copying a system template duplicates its linked resource files into the target tenant. export-bundle rejects a bundle whose locales differ in content format or variable schema with `bundleLocalesDiffer`.
  -->
- 15039ce: Template preview size budget and draft scope
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: fix
  title: Template preview counts encoding overhead and reports missing attachments
  detail: The mail size estimate counts base64 size plus a fixed per-part overhead, an attachment whose file reference is missing fails the resources_resolved check, and the document draft scope is derived once per request.
  -->
- 15039ce: The layout editor counts the users of a layout on the server instead of from a page of 200 templates
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: fix
  title: template-resolver:query:overview accepts layoutSlug to list only the mails and PDFs using that layout
  detail: The optional layoutSlug payload field keeps only documents whose layout slug matches; total counts the filtered rows. Without it the response is unchanged.
  -->
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: document-designer
  type: fix
  title: Layout editor shows the real number of mails or PDFs using a layout
  detail: The editor asks the overview for the users of one layout (kind and layoutSlug filter) and takes the count from total, so a tenant with more than 200 templates no longer sees a too low usage number.
  -->
- 15039ce: Template layout usage uses effective rows
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: fix
  title: Layout usage follows the effective template per notification and locale
  detail: Mail layout usage counts a notification only when it declares a template and resolves the effective row per notification and locale, so tenant overrides are reflected.
  -->
- fd5009a: Tenant job run state is keyed by tenant, job name and BullMQ job id
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: jobs
  type: fix
  title: Tenant-visible job runs no longer collide across tenants, jobs and lanes
  detail: store_tenant_job_runs was unique on bull_job_id alone, but BullMQ ids count per queue, so a job on the api lane and one on the worker lane (or two tenants after a Redis reset) shared an id and overwrote each other's row. The unique index now covers (tenant_id, job_name, bull_job_id), every write filters by all three, and an enqueue replaces a finished row left over under the same key. onJobDropped now receives { tenantId } as a third argument.
  migration: |
    Run `kumiko-schema generate` in your app to add the migration that creates store_tenant_job_runs_tenant_job_bull_job_id_unique and drops store_tenant_job_runs_bull_job_id_unique (generated as a commented DROP INDEX; uncomment it). A custom onJobDropped callback passed to the job runner now gets a third argument { tenantId }.
  -->
- 8e81d73: Tier assignment changes no longer reload the publishing process twice and stale reloads cannot overwrite a resync
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tier-engine
  type: fix
  title: Tier cache: stale single reload cannot overwrite a newer full resync
  detail: A single-tenant reload that started before a full resync and resolved after it could restore an outdated tier. The resync now advances the per-tenant ticket for deleted and adopted tenants too, and assignment changes are published remote-only.
  -->
- 8e81d73: update-tenant-field exposes the type field
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: custom-fields
  type: fix
  title: update-tenant-field no longer hides `type` from the handler schema
  detail: The `type` field is part of the documented payload; the 422 check against changing the stored type remains the protection.
  -->
- 8e81d73: Workflow failure logs show the original error
  
  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: workflow-runner
  type: fix
  title: Workflow run-failed and retry logs carry the original cause
  detail: The ops log used to print the generic `workflow step N failed` wrapper. It now prints the underlying error, while the persisted event still carries the error class only.
  -->

## 0.363.0

### Minor Changes

- 9120f65: Remove AuthMailContent from auth-email-password

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: breaking
  title: AuthMailContent is removed
  detail: The sections-based content type only fed the retired renderer-simple. Auth mails are template notifications with variables, so nothing builds or consumes AuthMailContent anymore.
  migration: |
    Drop AuthMailContent imports; the auth mail text lives in the seeded templates and is overridden per tenant in the template editor.
  -->

- ef689d8: Auth mails are stored templates rendered by renderer-mail-html

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: auth-email-password
  type: breaking
  title: Auth mails are notifications with seeded templates, render*Email is gone
  detail: password-reset, account-unlock, email-verification, signup-activation and invite are declared as r.notification with a localized template and variables, seeded as system templates at boot and rendered by renderer-mail-html, so a tenant can override the text in the template editor. A locale without its own subject key falls back to en, because the renderer has no locale fallback. AuthMailNotificationTypes is exported for the qualified names.
  migration: |
    The notification types are now `auth-email-password:notify:<name>` (before: the plain names). Update delivery preferences, preference rows and tests that reference the old names. renderResetPasswordEmail, renderUnlockAccountEmail, renderVerifyEmail, renderActivationEmail, renderInviteEmail, AuthMailSection, RenderTokenContentArgs and RenderInviteEmailArgs are removed; AuthMailContent stays. An app that mounts auth-email-password now needs template-resolver, renderer-foundation and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-mail-html (composeRendererStack() from dev-server mounts all of them; with includeBundled, composeFeatures adds whichever is missing). Boot fails with a clear error otherwise, and apps without the template tables need a schema migration (`kumiko schema generate`). kumiko-schema-check counts the three as implicit features of every HAS_AUTH app, so its check fails until that migration exists. Tests that read the token from a mail use the text part (`mail.text`); the html part encodes `=` as `&#x3D;`.
  -->

The notification types are qualified names now (billing-foundation:notify:<name>). The notify data is the template variable object (subject, details, contractLines, termsParagraphs, operatorEmail), not sections.

An app that mounts it without includeBundled needs template-resolver, renderer-foundation and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-mail-html at boot (composeRendererStack() from dev-server mounts all of them), plus a delivery with the channel-email feature; apps without the template tables need a schema migration (`kumiko schema generate`).

  feature: channel-email
  type: breaking

  detail: The renderer option of createChannelEmailFeature is removed. A notification routed to the email channel without template + meta fails its delivery permanently with "has no mail template, declare template + meta on r.notification". r.notification declares no channels, so this is not checked at boot; an app's own mail tests over the inmemory transport catch it.
  migration: |
    Drop the renderer option. Declare template + meta (or localizedTemplate) and variables on every r.notification that reaches the email channel, or accept that its email delivery fails. Run the app's notification tests after the bump: every email notification without a template now fails there.

- 9120f65: Inline delivery path passes the tenant config accessor

  feature: delivery
  type: breaking
  title: NotificationRenderer and RendererInput removed, immediate notify renders with the tenant config
  detail: The inline (immediate, job-less) delivery path now gets the tenant config accessor like the delivery.render job, so the mail layout shows the tenant name in both paths. DeliveryServiceOptions and CreateDeliveryTestContextOptions accept tenantConfigFor; runProdApp wires it from the boot config resolver. The types NotificationRenderer and RendererInput are removed from the delivery exports because the legacy renderer path is gone.
  migration: |
    Drop NotificationRenderer and RendererInput imports; render mails with template + meta on r.notification (see renderer-foundation).
  -->

- 58452ae: ctx.notify in write handlers delivers after commit

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: ctx.notify in write handlers delivers after commit
  detail: Inside a write handler's transaction ctx.notify only records the notification and delivers it once the write has committed, so a rolled-back write sends nothing and leaves no attempt event. Delivery no longer takes a connection from the app pool while the write holds one, which deadlocked at pool max N with N parallel writes. With immediate: true the call stays synchronous and runs its DB work on the outside-transaction pool.
  migration: |
    NotifyResult is now a union, NotifyDispatched ({ kind: "dispatched", deliveries }) or NotifyDeferred ({ kind: "deferred" }). In a write handler without immediate: true ctx.notify returns deferred and delivers after commit (a rollback means no notification). Code that reads the result (for example a "send test message" handler showing sent/failed) sets immediate: true, which delivers synchronously on the outside-transaction pool and returns dispatched; narrow on kind before reading deliveries. Errors such as a missing idempotency Redis, a tenant broadcast without the tenant feature or an unknown notification type no longer throw in a deferred write handler, they land in the afterCommit log. Notifications from jobs, from seeding and from handlers without a transaction stay synchronous. The boot default wires tenantUserIdsQuery for to: { tenant } when the tenant feature is mounted, so an app-side tenantUserIdsQuery wiring can go. Custom NotifyFactory implementations receive an optional 4th parameter deliveryDb, and DeliveryService.notify an optional 6th.
  -->

The job path passes the tenant config accessor to the renderer, the inline path renders without one.

  detail: ContentEditorFormat gains "document". template-resolver registers DocumentContentEditor for it (tiptap, lazy-loaded) and stores the body as html. Placeholders are inserted only as variable nodes (data-variable), never as {{name}} text. ContentPreview does not substitute example values for "document" content, because substituting a button or link href would make the schema drop that node. New exports from template-resolver/web: DocumentContentEditor, DocumentEditorProps, DocumentToolbarBlock, MAIL_DOCUMENT_BLOCKS, PDF_DOCUMENT_BLOCKS.

- b022cca: Document PDFs are rendered from stored templates by renderer-puppeteer-client

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer-foundation
  type: breaking
  title: document-pdf requests name a template, the response carries fileName
  detail: The document-pdf payload is { slug, locale, variables } instead of ready HTML in content. The response has a fileName, RendererContext gets an optional filesForTenant (file access per tenant) and RendererError has the new code unavailable for a renderer backend that cannot be reached.
  migration: |
    Callers that sent `payload: { content }` switch to a document-pdf template and pass slug, locale and variables (money-horse credit-schedule-pdf follows in #621); renderer-pdf callers pass slug and locale too. The enterprise package @cosmicdriftgamestudio/kumiko-renderer-puppeteer-client no longer builds against these types and is replaced by @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-puppeteer-client.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer-puppeteer-client
  type: breaking
  title: renders document-pdf from templates, adds renderAndStorePdf, the rendered-pdf entity and puppeteer-status
  detail: The plugin resolves the document-pdf template and its pdf-layout (header, signature, footer), embeds every image as a data URI and sends finished HTML to the puppeteer-service. renderAndStorePdf(ctx, { slug, locale, variables, attachTo? }) stores the PDF as a file and a rendered-pdf record with the template and layout version. The puppeteer-status query reports whether the service answers; while it does not, rendering fails with PuppeteerUnavailableError (HTTP 503, puppeteer_unavailable). The feature adds the table rendered_pdfs.
  migration: |
    Call renderAndStorePdf(ctx, { slug, locale, variables, attachTo? }) from a write handler; no escape hatch or rendererDb is needed because the tenant db also reads system templates and files. Apps that mount renderer-puppeteer-client need a schema migration for rendered_pdfs (`kumiko schema generate`). PUPPETEER_SERVICE_URL and PUPPETEER_AUTH_TOKEN stay as before. image-snapshot requests are unchanged.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: Mails can attach a PDF that is rendered from a document template when the mail is sent
  detail: notify data.attachments accepts { kind: "rendered-pdf", templateSlug, variables, fileName, locale? }. The send job renders the PDF through the document-pdf renderer, so the job payload carries the variables (at most 64000 bytes as JSON), not the bytes. Variables are stored in the job payload, so keep personal data out of them or accept that retention.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: channel-email
  type: improvement
  title: Email channel sends rendered-pdf attachments
  detail: The channel resolves rendered-pdf entries from notify data next to file entries; without a locale the message locale is used. A render failure fails the send job, so the retry runs it again.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer-mail-html
  type: improvement
  title: Images in layout regions, exported document-kit helpers
  detail: A mail layout region can contain images (data-resource) that are sent as inline attachments. The document helpers (createDocumentHandlebars, compileDocumentSource, readDocumentFormat, readTenantName, resolveResourceFileRefs, collectRegionResourceKeys, mergeResourceFileRefs) are exported, so other renderers format documents the same way.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer-puppeteer-client
  type: improvement
  title: The service performs no network fetches
  detail: Only data:, about: and blob: requests are allowed, everything else is aborted. The client embeds all resources as data URIs, so there is no DNS rebinding and no reachable node IP or kubelet. Margins accept 0.

  <!-- kumiko-changes

  detail: RendererPlugin gets the optional capability previewDocument(req, ctx), which returns the filled-in body and layout regions without calling the print service. template-resolver:query:preview with kind document-pdf uses it, so the editor shows replaced placeholders and the resource and required-placeholder checks; without such a plugin the preview keeps returning the body and raw layout.

- 4a748c3: ctx.notify rejects a broadcast to another tenant

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: ctx.notify rejects a broadcast to another tenant
  detail: A notify with to: { tenant } now throws an AccessDeniedError (reason notify_foreign_tenant_broadcast) unless the tenant is the caller's own, before any delivery work. In a write handler it fails synchronously instead of landing in the afterCommit log. Notifications fired from seed hooks during self-signup no longer use the app pool inside the signup transaction, which deadlocked at pool max N with N parallel signups; they deliver after commit. ctx.scheduleAfterCommit is now absent in query bridges and post-commit contexts, where hooks pushed to it never ran; callers that check for it (cache-sync announce, set-tenant-tier onAssigned, form-draft discard, seed hooks) now run inline there instead of being dropped.
  migration: |
    to: { tenant } must be the tenant of the caller (user.tenantId of the handler or job context), otherwise notify throws; in a write handler the throw is synchronous. Seed-hook notifications in the signup transaction run after commit and return { kind: "deferred" } (immediate: true runs synchronously on the outside-transaction pool, which cannot see rows the signup transaction has not committed yet, so a tenant broadcast there finds no new member). No known consumer broadcasts to a foreign tenant.
  -->

RendererContext gains an optional config accessor that plugins use for tenant locale, currency and branding.

- 9120f65: Remove renderer-simple, MailBranding and the renderer kind notification

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: renderer-foundation
  type: breaking
  title: renderer-simple, MailBranding and renderer kind "notification" are removed
  detail: Every mail is a stored template rendered by renderer-mail-html now. renderer-simple (createRendererSimpleFeature, simpleRenderer, createSimpleRenderer, RendererSimpleOptions, mail blocks with LocalizedText, MailBadge, MailChip, MailStage, MailStageState and MailTone), the MailBranding type, the renderer kind "notification" and AuthMailContent are gone. NotificationRenderer and RendererInput are removed from delivery, and createChannelEmailFeature no longer takes a renderer option. The type NotificationPayload is removed from renderer-foundation. The template-resolver keeps "notification" only as a stored kind so legacy rows stay readable; RENDER_KINDS is mail, document-pdf and image-snapshot.
  migration: |
    Remove createRendererSimpleFeature() and any renderer or mailBranding option from your feature list and createChannelEmailFeature call. An r.notification that is sent by email needs template + meta (or localizedTemplate) and variables; the sections/header/footer data it carried is replaced by template variables. Branding (logo, footer) now comes from the tenant branding config and the mail layout of renderer-mail-html. Mount template-resolver, renderer-foundation and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-renderer-mail-html (composeRendererStack() mounts all of them) and run seedNotificationTemplates at boot. Existing template rows with kind "notification" are no longer rendered; re-create them as kind "mail" or archive them.

- 7ed530a: Template bodies of kind mail-html and document-pdf with contentFormat html are rebuilt through a shared document schema on every write

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: template-resolver
  type: breaking
  title: document-pdf templates require contentFormat html, and html bodies are sanitized on write
  detail: upsertSystem, upsertTenant, the collection-set handlers and seedSystemTemplate rebuild html bodies of kind mail-html and document-pdf through the new document schema (template-resolver/document-schema). New exports: documentExtensions, DocumentLink and the other Document* nodes, isAllowedDocumentLinkHref, isDocumentReferenceName, isDocumentResourceKey, isDocumentPlaceholderHref, sanitizeDocumentHtml, sanitizeTemplateBody. kind document-pdf with another contentFormat is rejected with document_requires_html_format.

## 0.362.0

### Patch Changes

- e5c2657: document-ingest events live on their own stream

  documentIngest.requested/skipped were appended to the fileRef's own event stream (aggregateId = fileRefId), so the request-ingest projection racing a save that binds a pending upload broke the fileRef's optimistic lock (409 version_conflict). They now use documentIngestAggregateId(tenantId, fileRefId); payload.fileRefId is unchanged.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: document-ingest-foundation
  type: fix
  title: document-ingest events live on their own stream
  -->

- c455a6c: The source IP and user agent of rejected export-download attempts is now encrypted personal data. Job-path rows use the requesting user's key, anonymous token-path rows use the tenant key, and list-download-attempts still filters by IP through a blind index and returns plaintext IP and user agent.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: user-data-rights
  type: fix
  title: download-attempt.ip and userAgent are encrypted personal data instead of plaintext
  detail: |
    download-attempt.ip and userAgent are declared personal: { of: "attemptedByUserId", whenAbsent: "tenant" }, ip with find "exact" and userAgent with find "none". With a KMS configured, rows written by the logged-in job path are encrypted under the requesting user's key (a user forget makes IP and user agent unreadable), rows from the anonymous token path under the tenant key. The new ip_bidx column keeps the equality filter of list-download-attempts working across both kinds of rows, and the query now returns the decrypted values (an erased user's values come back as the erased sentinel). user-data-rights-defaults registers an EXT_USER_DATA hook for download-attempt: export lists the user's own attempts, delete purges the user's own attempts via the forget verb (projection row and blind index included, replayed on rebuild); owner-less token-path rows expire with the 90d hardDelete retention.
  migration: |
    Apps that mount user-data-rights run kumiko-schema generate and apply: the migration adds the ip_bidx column and its index to read_download_attempts. Apps that mount user-data-rights without user-data-rights-defaults must register their own EXT_USER_DATA hook for the download-attempt entity, otherwise boot fails the PII hook coverage check. The annotation fingerprint of the boot PII backfill changes, so the first boot after the bump does one full pass: it encrypts existing download-attempt events (tenant key or user key) and rebuilds the projection including ip_bidx (KUMIKO_SKIP_PII_BACKFILL=1 turns it off).
  -->

## 0.361.0

### Minor Changes

- a3a51aa: An edit field can be pre-filled when the create form opens. `{ field: "date", prefill: { kind: "today" } }` fills a date field with today's calendar date in the user's time zone, `{ field: "inspector", prefill: { kind: "currentUser", property: "displayName" } }` (or `email`, `id`) fills from the signed-in user. Only empty values are filled, the update form and values from URL params or a handoff are never touched, and unlike a field `default` nothing is applied server-side. The auth session now provides the user through the new `CurrentUserProvider` / `useOptionalCurrentUser()` renderer context, and `user:me` additionally returns `effectiveTimeZone`, the user's effective IANA zone (own setting, else tenant, else UTC); without a user zone the locale resolver's zone is used.

## 0.360.0

### Minor Changes

- cc46b78: Session cookies written Secure and without a Domain attribute now use the `__Host-` prefix: `__Host-kumiko_auth`, `__Host-kumiko_csrf` and `__Host-kumiko_tenant`. A browser only accepts such a cookie when it is Secure, Path=/ and host-only, so a sibling subdomain can no longer set or shadow it. With `auth.cookieDomain` or without Secure the plain names stay. The new auth option `secureCookies` forces the Secure flag (default: `NODE_ENV === "production"`); buildServer resolves it once.

  The base names and the naming rule live in `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/session-cookies` (`AUTH_COOKIE_BASE`, `CSRF_COOKIE_BASE`, `TENANT_COOKIE_BASE`, `sessionCookieName`, `resolveSessionCookieNames`). `readCsrfToken()` reads the prefixed csrf cookie first and falls back to the plain one.

  A request that carries the auth or the csrf cookie name twice is treated as having no session cookie (anonymous with `anonymousAccess`, otherwise 401) and the response expires every cookie variant, so a shadowed or stale duplicate can no longer pin a browser to the wrong session.

  The Origin guard now also runs without `allowedOrigins` when the app's public origin is known: the new auth option `publicOrigin`, which runProdApp fills from `auth.mail.baseUrl` and then from the `APP_BASE_URL` env. It admits that origin plus the request's own host. Without such a URL runProdApp warns at boot in production and keeps running.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Secure host-only session cookies use the __Host- prefix
  detail: Auth, csrf and tenant cookies are named __Host-kumiko_auth, __Host-kumiko_csrf and __Host-kumiko_tenant when they are written Secure and without a Domain (the tenant cookie is always host-only). With auth.cookieDomain or without Secure the auth and csrf names stay kumiko_auth and kumiko_csrf. New auth option secureCookies forces Secure (default NODE_ENV === "production"). Login deletes the legacy unprefixed host-only cookies, logout and deleteTenantCookie delete the prefixed and the legacy names. The server reads only the resolved names, so a request that carries only the legacy kumiko_auth is anonymous. AUTH_COOKIE_NAME, CSRF_COOKIE_NAME and TENANT_COOKIE_NAME are removed from the framework and dispatcher-live; the base names and sessionCookieName() are exported from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-types/session-cookies and @cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/api, getSessionCookies(c) returns the resolved names of a request. The testing package's CSRF_COOKIE_NAME stays and resolves to the unprefixed name (e2e servers run without Secure).
  migration: Every user logs in once after the deploy, because the old kumiko_auth cookie is no longer read. Custom clients, proxies or scripts that read or forward the cookies by literal name break: read the names through sessionCookieName() / resolveSessionCookieNames() (types package) or getSessionCookies(c) on the server, and handle both the prefixed and the plain name in browser code (readCsrfToken() already does). Replace imports of AUTH_COOKIE_NAME, CSRF_COOKIE_NAME and TENANT_COOKIE_NAME with AUTH_COOKIE_BASE, CSRF_COOKIE_BASE and TENANT_COOKIE_BASE plus sessionCookieName(); e2e helpers that imported CSRF_COOKIE_NAME from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-dispatcher-live import it from @cosmicdrift/kumiko-testing/e2e instead (known: solon e2e/_helpers/api.ts and e2e/session-ended.spec.ts, kumiko-enterprise ai-agent-live-transcription.integration.test.ts uses AUTH_COOKIE_NAME). A reverse proxy that strips or rewrites cookie names must pass the __Host- names unchanged. Staging or preview deployments over plain http need no change (Secure is off there); set auth.secureCookies (also accepted by runProdApp) explicitly when TLS terminates before the app and NODE_ENV is not "production". A standalone createAuthRoutes mount outside buildServer must also mount sessionCookiesMiddleware with the same resolved names, otherwise the readers fall back to the domain-less default.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: improvement
  title: Duplicate session cookie names end the cookie session
  detail: When the Cookie header carries the resolved auth or csrf cookie name more than once, authMiddleware ignores the cookie transport and expires every variant (prefixed host-only, legacy host-only, the cookieDomain variant and retired domains). With anonymousAccess the request continues as anonymous, otherwise it gets 401 missing_token; a Bearer token on the same request still authenticates. A prefixed and a legacy name side by side are not a duplicate. The cookie clearing moved from the auth routes into clearSessionCookies in session-cookies.ts; ResolvedSessionCookies carries domain and retiredDomains.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Origin guard defaults on when the public app URL is known
  detail: New auth option publicOrigin. Without allowedOrigins, cookieDomain and unsafeSkipOriginCheck, buildServer mounts the Origin guard for cookie-authenticated state-changing /api requests and admits publicOrigin plus the request's own host (Host header). runProdApp sets publicOrigin from auth.publicOrigin, then auth.mail.baseUrl, then the APP_BASE_URL env (origin only, path dropped); with none of them in production it logs a warning that the Origin guard is off and boots anyway. allowedOrigins keeps its strict meaning, and the WebSocket check and the anonymous downgrade still use only allowedOrigins.
  migration: Cookie-authenticated POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE requests from a page on another origin than the public app URL and than the API host itself now get 403 origin_not_allowed in runProdApp deployments that set auth.mail.baseUrl or APP_BASE_URL. A web client served from a different host than the API (for example a sibling subdomain) must list its origin in auth.allowedOrigins. Same-host setups, custom domains served by the same server and Bearer clients need no change.
  -->

- b0e8bd3: New `renderer-pdf` bundled feature: `renderTablePdf(doc)` draws a table document as a PDF in pure JavaScript (pdf-lib, no browser, no native dependency). The document has a title, meta lines, weighted columns, cell wrapping, a header row repeated on every page and a footer with page numbers. `createRendererPdfFeature()` registers it as the `pdf` plugin for `kind: "document-pdf"` in `renderer-foundation`. Recipe: `samples/recipes/pdf-audit-export`.

  `createFileRefFromBytes(ctx, { fileName, mimeType, data, attachTo? })` from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/files` stores bytes a write handler or job produced itself as a FileRef. It runs the same pipeline as `POST /api/files`, which now calls it too. That covers the identifier check, field resolution, size and accept limits, content sniffing and the MIME allowlist, the tenant-bound storage key and the `fileRef.created` event. Rejections come back as 422 `file_rejected` with the upload error in `details.error`.

  `createImagesField({ capture })` forwards `capture` to the edit view model the same way `createImageField` does.

  Cron jobs take an optional IANA time zone: `trigger: { cron: "0 7 * * *", tz: "Europe/Berlin" }`. Boot aborts for an invalid zone.

  `createUserProfileFeature({ allowEmailChange: false })` drops the `change-email` handler and the email section of the profile screen. The default keeps both.

Characters outside WinAnsi are replaced by "?". Identical input yields identical bytes. createRendererPdfFeature() registers it as plugin "pdf" for kind "document-pdf"; payload.variables is validated against pdfTableDocumentSchema, anything else fails with RendererError invalid_payload.
  -->

The tenant always comes from ctx.user. A rejected file returns a 422 write failure with reason file_rejected and the upload error string in details.error. The FileRef's insertedById is the passed user, so the default access guard lets only that user and privileged roles read files attached to an entity.

- e71b639: A finished tenant job run replaces the older finished run of the same subject in one transaction, so the run store never holds two finished rows for one subject.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: jobs
  type: fix
  title: Finished tenant job run replaces the older one atomically
  detail: recordTenantRunOutcome wrote the new completed or failed row and pruned older finished rows of the same tenant, job and subject in two separate statements, so the store briefly held two finished rows per subject, and two runs of one subject finishing together could each miss the other's row and leave both. Both writes now run in one transaction under a per-key advisory lock (namespace tjrl). jobs:query:tenant-runs already showed only the newest finished row, so its result does not change.
  -->

- bea04fb: cap-counter: reserveCalendarCapUsage reserves capacity before an expensive call and settles the actual usage afterwards, from handlers and jobs

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: cap-counter
  type: improvement
  title: Reserve and settle cap usage outside the dispatcher
  detail: |
    reserveCalendarCapUsage(ctx, { capName, periodStartIso, limit, profile, amount, notify? }) runs the same sweep, soft-hit notification and guarded hard-cap reservation as withCapEnforcement and returns a handle. settle(actualAmount) replaces the reserved amount by the actual one in one transaction (and books the full actual amount if the reservation was swept or released meanwhile); release() gives it back. Parallel callers cannot exceed the hard cap. It works with a HandlerContext (also r.systemScope() handlers) and a JobContext. Pattern: `const r = await reserveCalendarCapUsage(ctx, {...}); try { ...; await r.settle(actual) } catch (e) { await r.release(); throw e }`. bookCapUsage, markCapSoftWarned, releaseCapUsage and the enforceCap family accept a JobContext as well.
  migration: |
    withCapEnforcement and bookCapUsage now work on r.systemScope() handlers; before, they failed on the fail-closed ctx.db. Reservation rows carry the tenant of ctx.user explicitly, and a context whose tenant-mode db belongs to another tenant than ctx.user is rejected with access_denied. enforceCap now filters the counter by ctx.user.tenantId, so a system-mode db no longer reads another tenant's counter.

  feature: framework
  type: breaking
  title: Entity PII fields need whenAbsent: "tenant" when the owner field is nullable
  detail: |
    personal: { of: "<owner>", whenAbsent: "tenant" } makes rows without an owner editable, deletable and forgettable with an active KMS, without plaintext PII. The subject is resolved in this order: the owner on the previous row, the owner the same event sets, then the tenant key (tenant:<tenantId>). Before, an update, delete or forget of an ownerless row failed with SubjectResolutionError (HTTP 500) once a KMS was configured. backfill-pii follows the same chain and checks the projection row for the owner before it falls back to the tenant key; an updated event whose previous.owner is null but whose changes.owner is set no longer loses the owner. Entity fields have no plaintext fallback, so "tenant" is the only value. bundled jobs: cron and system runs (triggeredById null) now store payload, error and log messages as ciphertext under the system tenant key instead of plaintext.
  migration: |
    Boot now aborts for a personal: { of: "<owner>" } field whose owner field is not required and that declares no whenAbsent: [Feature X] Field "f" on entity "e" is personal: { of: "ownerId" }, but "ownerId" is not required — rows without an owner would fail to encrypt (SubjectResolutionError, HTTP 500) on update, delete and forget. Declare { personal: { of: "ownerId", whenAbsent: "tenant" } } to encrypt those rows under the tenant key, or make "ownerId" required: true. Entity fields have no plaintext fallback (fw#3654). Fix: add whenAbsent: "tenant", or make the owner field required: true if every row has one. whenAbsent on personal: { of: "id" } throws at declaration. Known consumer sites: kumiko-enterprise kumiko-credit entity.ts and bauspar-entity.ts (ownerUserId), ai-agent entity.ts (authorId, ownerId) and attachment-store.ts (authorId), ai-conversation entity.ts (authorId), pattern-storage entity.ts (authorId), offlot-app src/features/lead/schema/entity.ts (enquiryId). Existing plaintext job-run rows of cron runs stay readable; new ones are ciphertext.

## 0.357.0

### Minor Changes

- 03b6438: Delivery idempotencyKey is released when nothing was delivered

  A retry of a failed notify() with the same idempotencyKey is no longer skipped as a duplicate. The key is deleted when no recipient got a `sent` or `queued` delivery, also when notify() throws; one successful recipient keeps it, even if notify() throws afterwards (a retry would re-send to them). For queued channels the send/render job deletes the key after its final failed attempt, not per retry. That reference is only attached when a `route` call has exactly one channel address; `to` calls (user lists) and multi-channel routes keep the key after queueing. The job payload gains an optional `idempotencyKey`, backward compatible. `createDeliveryTestContext` accepts `idempotencyRedis`.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: delivery
  type: improvement
  title: Delivery idempotencyKey is released when nothing was delivered
  -->

- 1ed997b: forget-subject shreds note bodies attached to the subject and notes that mention it

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: crypto-shredding
  type: improvement
  title: forget-subject shreds note bodies attached to the subject and notes that mention it
  detail: |
    `forget-subject` on a user or record subject now also erases the per-note keys of every `note-entry` that hangs on the subject as host entity (entityId, plus entityType for record subjects) or @-mentions it, unless the host entity's retention strategy is anonymize/blockDelete. The automated Art. 17 delete hook reaches notes on the user as host too, and the export lists them. Before, `forget-subject(contact)` left the note bodies readable. Consumer tests that expect readable note bodies after `forget-subject` on a contact (e.g. solon contact-notes-forget) now see the erased sentinel. Forgetting only the author still leaves the bodies readable.
  -->

- d7872bd: Multi-select options can be hidden per caller, and the member roles form only offers assignable roles

  `MultiSelectFieldDef.optionsAvailabilityQuery` names a query that returns `{ rows: { value, disabled?, hint? }[] }`, called with an empty payload. The renderer hides every option whose row has `disabled: true`, in the combobox and in the `display: "checkboxes"` grid, unless the value is currently selected. `hint` is ignored because the combobox cannot show a per-option hint. Static `options` stay authoritative, and until the result arrives or when the query fails all options are shown, so the write path still has to enforce the rule. Boot fails when the query is empty or not a registered query handler, on entity fields and on form screen fields.

  The tenant feature registers `tenant:query:member-role-availability` and wires it to the `roles` field of `memberRolesEditScreen`. An Admin no longer sees TenantAdmin or an app role declared with `assignableFrom: "TenantAdmin"`; a TenantAdmin sees every role. The rank rule is the one `updateMemberRoles` already enforces, so the server behaviour is unchanged.

- a2bafb2: Handler titles and field labels as an i18n convention, plus the `references` Zod meta

  - `handlerTitleKey(qn)` gives `<qn>:title`, `handlerFieldLabelKey(qn, field)` gives `<qn>:field:<field>`. Exported from `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine` and `@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/ui-types`. The client resolves keys verbatim, so a feature writes the full keys in `r.translations`, e.g. `channel-texts:write:generate:title` and `channel-texts:write:generate:field:vehicleId`, best built with `handlerTitleKey(qn)`.
  - A translation key that already starts with the kebab form of the feature name (`channel-texts:write:x:title` for `channelTexts`) is no longer prefixed a second time.
  - `handlerFieldReference(schema, field)` and `HANDLER_FIELD_REFERENCES_META_KEY` (`@cosmicdrift/kumiko-framework/engine`) read `.meta({ references: "<entity>" })` on a handler input field, through optional, nullable and default wrappers. Boot fails when the value names no registered entity (`"<entity>"` or `"<feature>:<entity>"`). The value also appears in the agent tool JSON Schema.
  - `findHandlerTranslationGaps(features)` (`@cosmicdrift/kumiko-bundled-features/agent-tools`) reports `handler-without-translation` for agent-exposed write handlers without an entity mapping or actionForm screen that lack title or field-label keys (system-only fields are skipped). `kumiko agent lint` prints these in a separate warning section that never changes the exit code; the boot prints a single summary line. `findAgentDocGaps` is deliberately unchanged, because the agent-manifest guard fails hard on every gap it returns.

- c10805f: Tenant-visible job run state: `r.job({ tenantVisibleRun })` plus `jobs:query:tenant-runs`

  A tenant can read whether work for a subject is queued or running, with its times, and the last completed or failed run. Counterpart to `tenantVisibleFailure`, without payloads, error texts or logs.

  - `JobDefinition.tenantVisibleRun: { subjectFields? }`: opt in per job. `subjectFields` name primitive payload fields that scope the state (stored in clear, never a PII field). A non-primitive value fails the run, as for `tenantVisibleFailure`.
  - New table `store_tenant_job_runs`: run `kumiko-schema generate <name>` in your app and apply the migration (`kumiko-schema apply`). It stays empty until a job opts in.
  - `jobs:query:tenant-runs` (payload `{ jobName?, subject?, limit? }`, every membership rank, own tenant only) returns `{ rows: [{ jobName, subject, status, queuedAt, startedAt, finishedAt }], nextCursor: null }`: all queued and running runs plus the latest completed or failed one per job and subject, active runs first.
  - A failed attempt that BullMQ retries shows as `queued` again; only the final failure shows `failed`. The stale-run sweep fails `running` rows and drops `queued` rows older than `staleRunTimeoutHours`; `retention-cleanup` purges finished rows older than `retentionDays`.
  - `JobRunnerOptions` gains optional `onJobQueued(jobName, jobId, { tenantId, subject })` and `onJobDropped(jobName, jobId)`; `JobMeta.tenantVisibleRun` and `JobOutcomeMeta.tenantVisibleRun` carry the subject to `onJobStart`/`onJobComplete`/`onJobFailed`. `jobRunLoggerCallbacks` and the test stack wire them automatically; existing callbacks keep working.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: jobs
  type: improvement
  title: Tenant-visible job run state: r.job({ tenantVisibleRun }) plus jobs:query:tenant-runs
  detail: A job that declares `tenantVisibleRun` keeps its queued, running, completed and failed state per tenant and subject in the new table `store_tenant_job_runs`, and the tenant reads it through `jobs:query:tenant-runs` (payload `{ jobName?, subject?, limit? }`, own tenant only). Each row is `{ jobName, subject, status, queuedAt, startedAt, finishedAt }`: every queued or running run plus the latest completed or failed one per job and subject, active runs first. No payload, error text or log ever reaches the tenant. A failed attempt that is retried shows as `queued` again. The stale-run sweep and `retention-cleanup` also cover the new table. `JobRunnerOptions` gains `onJobQueued` and `onJobDropped`.
  migration: New store table. Run `kumiko-schema generate <name>` and apply the migration with `kumiko-schema apply` - `store_tenant_job_runs` is created empty and stays empty until a job declares `tenantVisibleRun`. No change needed for apps that do not opt in.
  -->

- fde53b0: Reference fields can opt out of the handover with handover: "stay"; boot depth limit and mover share one graph definition

  ReferenceFieldDef gains handover: "stay". An entity that should NOT travel with its host but points at it through a plain reference no longer blocks the claim with entity_not_transferable when that reference field carries handover: "stay": the edge is not walked, its rows stay in the source tenant, and the reference crosses the tenant boundary after the handover. Without the opt-out the behaviour is unchanged (entity_not_transferable at claim time). Migration: an entity that should NOT travel with its host: mark the reference field handover: "stay" (removing transferable alone does not help once rows exist, the claim still fails). The framework now exports one adjacency definition (resolveEntityTransferAdjacency, reference and parentRef edges, non-transferable intermediate nodes included, handover: "stay" respected) that the boot validator's depth limit and the tenant-handover mover both use. Consequence: the boot-time MAX_TRANSFER_DEPTH check now also counts parentRef edges and chains running through non-transferable entities, as the mover always did; a graph that was deeper than 5 hops only through such nodes now fails the boot instead of the claim.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant-handover
  type: improvement
  title: Reference fields can opt out of the handover with handover: "stay"; boot depth limit and mover share one graph definition
  -->

Action: mount createFilesTenantDataFeature(), or ignore the warning if the app erases files itself.

### Patch Changes

- a734025: forget-subject: the SUBJECT_FORGOTTEN audit now commits before the handler tx does and records cleanupError when a derived-data sweep fails

  The SUBJECT_FORGOTTEN audit event is appended through the outside-transaction db, so it commits before the handler transaction does and survives a later rollback. If the blind-index sweep or search purge fails, the event carries cleanupError (error code or name, never the message) and the handler then fails; retry to finish the cleanup. The user-lifecycle step runs in a savepoint and no longer aborts the handler transaction.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: crypto-shredding
  type: fix
  title: forget-subject: the SUBJECT_FORGOTTEN audit now commits before the handler tx does and records cleanupError when a derived-data sweep fails
  -->

- fde53b0: folder:delete removes assignments whose host entity is gone instead of refusing forever

  An assignment pointing at a hard-deleted, soft-deleted or unregistered host blocked folder:delete permanently with folder_has_assignments, because clear-folder needs a visible host and could not remove it. folder:delete now removes such assignments through the event-store executor (normal delete events) before the check, without the caller's read gate. Assignments of live hosts, including ones the caller cannot see, still block with folder_has_assignments. A refused delete removes nothing. The cleanup runs lazily at folder:delete, not in a host-delete hook, so restoring a soft-deleted host before then keeps its folder.

  feature: folders
  type: fix
  title: folder:delete removes assignments whose host entity is gone instead of refusing forever
  -->

- a62e62c: Database, event-store consumer, search and Redis review fixes

  `db.global(table)` writes are rejected on executor-managed entity tables, and `unsafeRaw` handles derived through `begin`, `transaction` or `reserve` keep the personal-data gate. Reference sorting and search re-check label and read access plus ownership, and a stale search index can no longer surface another tenant's row. A cross-tenant convention handler reports one audit event per touched row with that row as target.

  A failing dispatcher pass no longer records its error on a consumer whose cursor moved in the meantime and skips a row another pass holds locked. A projection rebuild aborts when the configured blind-index key differs from the one used to build the live table. An array `ne` filter on a jsonb column means "does not contain all of these", matching the entity list filter. `date` columns that still hold a timestamptz log a warning once per column.

  `kumiko_event_dispatcher_listen_connected` only drops to 0 on a real connection-loss error and is restored when the pre-check recovers. A consumer logs once when it tracks more than 1000 pending gap ranges. The lazy Meilisearch default config no longer overwrites settings stored by an earlier `configure()` after a restart.

  Access invalidation publishes through `PubSubSignal.publishConfirmed`, so a Redis failure fails the consumer and the event is redelivered instead of being dropped (`SseBroker.publishAccessInvalidation` may return a promise). `KUMIKO_REDIS_CHANNEL_PREFIX` namespaces the SSE and feature-toggle Pub/Sub channels for apps sharing one Redis; `createRedisToggleSyncSignal` takes the prefix as an optional third argument. Types that mention `Temporal` now carry the `temporal-polyfill/global` reference into their `.d.ts` files.

- 6bd7df1: Final review batch D.

  - `FileHandle.derive(suffix)` now throws unless the suffix is `<name>-<16 hex>` (build it with `variantSuffix(name, spec)`). Free-form suffixes such as `derive("thumb")` wrote keys the forget/tenant-destroy sweep could not recognize, so those binaries survived erasure. Callers passing a bare name must switch to `variantSuffix`.
  - `resolveKmsWiring` / `requireKmsWiring` throw when a `*_CIPHERTEXT` slot is set without its plaintext, pointing at the async entry points, instead of a misleading "trio required" error or a silent plaintext-PII fallback.
  - Event-PII owner/`whenAbsent` resolution now also runs without a configured KMS, so a missing owner fails in dev like in prod.
  - PII event backfill queues rebuilds under a per-run migration id, so a peer replica's re-queue is no longer cleared by another run.
  - `seedAdminGuarded` re-writes the canonical admin's email so the blind index is repaired, and skips undecryptable foreign user rows instead of aborting the boot seed.
  - A tenant-bound `FileContext.list` refuses prefixes outside the tenant's key space.
  - An entityList whose create screen was dropped for the caller's roles now carries `createUnavailable`, so the renderer no longer falls back to a generic create form.
  - Boot validation rejects an object-form `redirect` with `idFrom` whose same-feature target screen carries no id.
  - `defineFeature` throws when `dedupeOptions` holds a nested object (it can never compare equal across two mounts).
  - `FileContext.ref` and `list` (tenant-bound) refuse keys outside `${tenantId}/`; list columns accept `virtual: true`; `httpRoute` session-only routes now pass the global IP rate limit; tenant timezone cache TTL is 30 s; text fields without a personal stance warn at boot; the orphan-derivative sweep keeps derivatives whose original still exists; `piiFields` owner fields that can never yield a string throw unless `whenAbsent` is set.

  A write that has to encrypt a personal field for a subject whose key was erased (crypto-shredding) now fails with a `ConflictError` (409, reason `subject_erased`, i18n in en and de) instead of a 500, on the executor write path and in `encryptForDirectWrite`. A hook's own `unsafeRaw` grant (`withUnsafeRawGrant`) no longer carries the handler's `globalWrites` grant. The job runner starts its BullMQ worker only after the boot gates passed, so a job queued by a previous run cannot execute against an unmet boot precondition. `buildServer` warns at boot when `r.systemScope()` features exist but no RateLimitResolver is configured. - 2b0566a: Tenant destroy stages resume partial progress in the next sweep tick instead of burning failed attempts

  A tenant with tens of thousands of files used to exhaust the stage's three attempts and leave the DSGVO destroy stuck. Destroy hooks (`destroyTenant`, EXT_TENANT_DATA `destroy`) may now return `{ done: false, processed }` and receive `deadlineAt` in their ctx; the runner records a `tenant-destruction-stage-progressed` event in the tenant stream and continues the stage next tick without counting a failed attempt. Hooks returning nothing stay valid. The `fileRef` row purge and the storage prefix wipe work in chunks against that deadline.

## 0.353.0

### Minor Changes

- b5466a7: Tenant names are PII encrypted under the tenant record and crypto-shredded on tenant destroy

  `tenant.name` is now `personal: { of: "id" }`, so it is stored as `kumiko-pii:` ciphertext in events and in `read_tenants`. Signup no longer writes the email into the tenant name; it uses the generated tenant key. The tenant destroy job erases the tenant record key and purges the tenant's search documents. The tenant queries (`me`, memberships, tenant-directory, user list, cap-overview, tenants-missing-profile) decrypt the name, and the tenant list sorts by `key` because encrypted names are not sortable.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant
  type: breaking
  title: Tenant names are encrypted under the tenant record and crypto-shredded when the tenant is destroyed
  migration: After the bump run the PII backfill (backfillEventPiiEncryption), then rebuild the read_tenants projection; the backfill only encrypts event payloads. Raw reads of read_tenants.name in apps now return ciphertext and must go through decryptStoredPii or the tenant query handlers. Tenants that were already destroyed (read_tenants.destroyed_at set) get the erased sentinel instead of a fresh record key.
  -->

### Patch Changes

- 4d6ce00: Managed pages and sitemap answer 429 when rate limited, agent catalog checks the deny list, draft cleanup continues past skipped rows

  A rate-limited managed-page request now answers 429 with `Retry-After` instead of 503 or an unbranded page, and `sitemap.xml` and `llms.txt` answer 429 instead of silently dropping the managed-page entries. `buildToolCatalog` throws when its manifest was built with `denyQns` that the catalog options lack. The form-draft cleanup no longer stops when a whole batch was re-saved by users in the meantime.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: managed-pages
  type: fix
  title: A rate-limited page request answers 429 with Retry-After instead of 503 or an unbranded page
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: seo
  type: fix
  title: sitemap.xml and llms.txt answer 429 when the managed-pages read is rate limited instead of omitting the pages
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: agent-tools
  type: fix
  title: buildToolCatalog throws when the manifest was built with denyQns the catalog options lack
  migration: Pass the same denyQns list to buildAgentManifest and buildToolCatalog.
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: form-draft
  type: fix
  title: The stale-draft cleanup keeps sweeping when a whole batch was re-saved in the meantime
  -->

- e1862ae: Agent manifest screen titles no longer depend on feature mount order

  Two features with a screen of the same short id used to get the title of whichever feature was mounted first. The manifest now looks up the screen's own feature-prefixed title key first and falls back to the unprefixed key.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: agent-tools
  type: fix
  title: Agent manifest screen titles resolve per feature instead of by mount order
  -->

- e1862ae: Audit list pages forward without repeats when sorted ascending

  `audit:query:list` with `sortDirection: "asc"` returned the same rows again on the next page because the cursor always meant "older than". The cursor now follows the sort direction, and ties are broken by event id. Sorting by `type` returns a single page without `nextCursor`, since an event id cannot resume a type-ordered listing.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: audit
  type: fix
  title: Audit list paging no longer repeats rows with ascending sort
  -->

- 4ec1c59: Tenant handover only fails with `transfer_graph_too_deep` when rows really hang below the fifth hop, and failed workflow runs report the suspended step

  A claim used to fail whenever the last round's entity type had outgoing edges, even with no rows behind them, so a chain of exactly five hops with an unrestricted `parentRef` entity registered was rejected. `workflow.run-failed` carries the real `stepIndex` for the unsupported-suspension case instead of always 0.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: tenant-handover
  type: fix
  title: Tenant handover claims fail with transfer_graph_too_deep only when rows exist beyond the last allowed hop
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: workflow-runner
  type: fix
  title: workflow.run-failed carries the real stepIndex when a run suspends in an unsupported step
  -->

- d32c9b3: Stricter boot checks and role projection for screens and handlers

  Inline handler registration without `options.access` now throws immediately, a section with `fields: []` and `groups: []` fails boot, and unknown tones in `header.statusTones` or select `optionTones` fail boot instead of dropping the badge colour. The renderer falls back to the value heuristic for an unknown tone, and `statusToneForOptionTone` now returns `undefined` for it. `secretMint` confirm-step actions are stripped for roles that cannot see the target screen.

  Entity convention `create` handlers keep tenant-filtered lookups even when the handler declares `escapeHatch`/`crossTenant`. Duplicate `waitForEvent` steps on the same `awaits` event are rejected when the workflow pipeline is built. An empty `PROMETHEUS_METRICS_TOKEN` counts as unset instead of failing boot.

  `GET /api/sse` now closes itself when the JWT it was opened with expires. File uploads must attach to a registered file field (a non-file field answers 400 `unresolvable_field`), and a `.docx` upload must be a ZIP containing `word/` entries. Signature extra routes outside `/api` get the request-body cap (`maxRequestBytes`) before their body is read. `EXT_USER_DATA` registrations with neither an export nor a delete hook fail boot. The dashboard updated-at stamp follows live refetches and retries.

  Text fields accept `minLength` (enforced by the generated write schema), `enumOption` renders array values per entry, list columns can opt out of sorting with `sortable: false`, and `BUILT_IN_MEMBERSHIP_ROLES` exposes the ranked membership roles. The PAT list translates its scopes column, MFA code fields enforce their minimum length, plan checkout no longer repeats the billing-enabled and active-subscription gates.

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Unknown status tones fail boot and secretMint confirm actions respect role gating
  -->

  `jobs:query:list` (job-runs screen) now pages with a `cursor` and returns `nextCursor` while older runs exist. Ledger `create-transaction` requires `subjectType` and `subjectId` together and rejects empty strings (also on schedule fields). The form-draft sweep re-check is tenant-scoped. A workflow run resumed without a stored definition fingerprint logs a warning.

  `EventDef.piiFields` is now required in the type, screen definitions accept only `agent: { expose }` (`AgentScreenHints`), and `FormController.validate(scope)` rejects field names that the form values do not have. The dedupe doc and the security-baseline recipe note that late-bound state (sessions auto-revoke) binds on the kept instance.

  A text or longText field with `multiline.rows` that is not a positive integer now fails the app-schema build with the entity or screen and field name instead of silently rendering four rows. List columns of type multiSelect render one pill per value like select columns. `config:query:values` accepts an optional `keys` list, and the tenant-currency lookup of money fields asks for its one key only.

  `createKumikoApp` accepts `schemaUrl` for the schema fetch when the API lives on another origin than the SPA (a cross-origin URL is fetched with `credentials: "include"`). List select cells and a danger `Dialog` now follow the registered primitives: select pills use the registered `StatusBadge`, and a danger dialog focuses Cancel by default. Form drafts no longer store fields marked `sensitive: true`.

  German and Spanish translations for `jobs.errors.invalidCursor` were missing.

  The release workflow waits for npm `latest` only on the packages the changesets run actually published and skips packages published under another dist-tag. `check:dist` compiles the installed `styles.css` and fails when classes from renderer-web or the renderer's compiled dist are missing.

## 0.352.0

### Minor Changes

- 9fb0657: Cap reservations run after every pre-handler gate and settle with the handler transaction

  Handlers wrapped with `withCapEnforcement` used to reserve capacity before rate limits, access and payload validation had run, so a rejected caller could use up cap or trigger a soft-warn. The dispatcher now runs the same gates, billing rate limits once, before it calls `reserveBeforeTransaction`; a failing gate rejects the command and releases the reservations taken before it. A hook that returns a `ReservationHandle` also confirms inside the handler transaction after the handler succeeded, and a confirm failure fails the write.

  Calendar reservations are now rows in the new `store_cap_reservations` table: the counter increment and the row commit together, the handler transaction deletes the row on its own commit, and a release only gives back what is still booked. Rolling caps reserve the same way: a version-guarded `rolling-incremented` append plus a reservation row before the handler transaction, undone by the new `cap-counter:event:rolling-released` event. `readRollingCapUsage` returns incremented minus released amounts in the window, never below 0. Rows a crashed process left behind expire after 60 minutes and are given back before the next reserve for the same cap. `withCapEnforcement` keeps the wrapped handler's other settings and chains an existing `reserveBeforeTransaction` of that handler: the inner reservation is taken first and given back if the outer one fails.

  feature: cap-counter
  type: breaking
  title: Calendar cap reservations are stored in the new store_cap_reservations table
  detail: Capped writes now insert and delete rows in store_cap_reservations, so they fail until the table exists.
  migration: Generate and apply a migration with `kumiko-schema generate` — capped writes fail without the new store_cap_reservations table
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
  feature: framework
  type: fix
  title: Rate-limited, denied or invalid callers no longer consume cap usage or trigger soft-warn, because pre-handler gates run before reserveBeforeTransaction
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes

  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes

  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes

  type: fix
  title: withCapEnforcement keeps the wrapped handler's settings (rateLimit, additionalRateLimits) and composes with an inner reserveBeforeTransaction
  -->

  <!-- kumiko-changes
